name: compose_with_bridge
doc:
**两段组合需要桥**：若段 `f` 保持 `P`、段 `g` 保持 `Q`，
且 `P` 在转手点蕴含 `Q`，则末端满足 `Q`。

**桥 `hbridge` 不可省**——见 `bridge_is_necessary`。
stmt:
theorem compose_with_bridge {α : Type} (P Q : α → Prop) (f g : α → α)
    (hf : ∀ x, P x → P (f x)) (hg : ∀ x, Q x → Q (g x))
    (hbridge : ∀ x, P x → Q x)
    (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    Q (g (f x))
proof: hg (f x) (hbridge (f x) (hf x hx))

name: compose_three_with_bridges
doc:
**多段 + 逐段桥**：每段保持自己的性质，每对相邻性质之间有一座桥。

这是**非相邻组合的一般形式**：段数不限，但每两次转手都需要一座桥。
stmt:
theorem compose_three_with_bridges {α : Type} (P Q R : α → Prop)
    (f g h : α → α)
    (hf : ∀ x, P x → P (f x)) (hg : ∀ x, Q x → Q (g x)) (hh : ∀ x, R x → R (h x))
    (hPQ : ∀ x, P x → Q x) (hQR : ∀ x, Q x → R x)
    (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    R (h (g (f x)))
proof: hh (g (f x)) (hQR _ (hg (f x) (hPQ _ (hf x hx))))

name: bridge_is_necessary
doc:
**没有桥时，两段组合的结论不成立。**

反例：取 `α = ℕ`、`P x := x = 0`、`Q x := x = 1`、`f := id`、`g := id`。
则 `P`、`Q` 各自被 `id` 保持，但 `P 0` 成立而 `Q 0` 不成立。

⇒ **`ClauseComposition` 原边界声明「应当由传递性得到」过强。**
非相邻组合**需要一条桥**，不是免费得到。
stmt:
theorem bridge_is_necessary :
    ¬ (∀ (P Q : ℕ → Prop) (f g : ℕ → ℕ),
        (∀ x, P x → P (f x)) → (∀ x, Q x → Q (g x)) →
        ∀ x, P x → Q (g (f x)))
proof:
by
  intro h
  have hinst := h (fun x => x = 0) (fun x => x = 1) id id
    (fun _ hx => hx) (fun _ hx => hx) 0 rfl
  norm_num at hinst

end BridgedComposition

end Lattice.Audit

name: preserves_foldl
doc:
**传递性：逐阶段保持 ⟹ 整体保持。**

给定阶段列表 `steps : List (α → α)`，若每个阶段都保持性质 `P`，
则把这些阶段依次施加到 `x` 上之后 `P` 仍成立。

这是「链路可组合」的**一般形式**：它不假设阶段之间有任何关系，
只要求每段各自保持同一性质。于是任意多段都能串起来，
不必为每一对相邻条款单独论证。
stmt:
theorem preserves_foldl {α : Type} (P : α → Prop)
    (steps : List (α → α)) (hstep : ∀ f ∈ steps, ∀ x, P x → P (f x))
    (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    P (steps.foldl (fun acc f => f acc) x)
proof:
by
  induction steps generalizing x with
  | nil => exact hx
  | cons f rest ih =>
    apply ih
    · intro g hg
      exact hstep g (List.mem_cons_of_mem f hg)
    · exact hstep f (List.mem_cons_self f rest) x hx

name: preserves_two
doc: **两段是特例**：`[f, g]` 的整体保持。
stmt:
theorem preserves_two {α : Type} (P : α → Prop) (f g : α → α)
    (hf : ∀ x, P x → P (f x)) (hg : ∀ x, P x → P (g x)) (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    P (g (f x))
proof: hg (f x) (hf x hx)

name: preserves_three
stmt:
theorem preserves_three {α : Type} (P : α → Prop) (f g h : α → α)
    (hf : ∀ x, P x → P (f x)) (hg : ∀ x, P x → P (g x)) (hh : ∀ x, P x → P (h x))
    (x : α) (hx : P x) : P (h (g (f x)))
proof:
hh (g (f x)) (hg (f x) (hf x hx))

end ChainTransitivity

namespace IterateForm

name: preserves_iterate
doc:
**迭代形式的保持律**：这是修复回路**实际使用**的形状。

`Nat.iterate f n` 与 `List.foldl` 是同一个想法的两个组合子，
但**类型不同**。一般定理不能直接套到回路上——这一点值得记录，
因为它说明「一般化」不等于「可套用」。
stmt:
theorem preserves_iterate {α : Type} (P : α → Prop) (f : α → α)
    (hf : ∀ x, P x → P (f x)) (n : ℕ) (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    P (Nat.iterate f n x)
proof:
by
  induction n generalizing x with
  | zero => exact hx
  | succ m ih => exact ih (f x) (hf x hx)

name: iterate_from_fold
doc:
**折叠形式蕴含迭代形式**（对常值阶段列表）。

两种形状**等价**：`foldl` 版本不更强，也不更弱，只是写在另一个组合子上。
stmt:
theorem iterate_from_fold {α : Type} (P : α → Prop) (f : α → α)
    (hf : ∀ x, P x → P (f x)) (n : ℕ) (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    P ((List.replicate n f).foldl (fun acc g => g acc) x)
proof:
ChainTransitivity.preserves_foldl P (List.replicate n f)
    (fun g _ y hy => by
      have hgf : g = f := List.eq_of_mem_replicate ‹g ∈ List.replicate n f›
      rw [hgf]; exact hf y hy)
    x hx

name: loop_preserves
doc:
**吸收律给出回路的保持律**：`Repair.preserves` 就是本定理在
`P := R.Sat`、`f := R.fix` 处的实例。

这条把一般定理**接到库自身的法则**上，证明实例化是真实的而非形式上的。
stmt:
theorem loop_preserves {α : Type} (R : Lattice.Core.Repair α) (n : ℕ) (x : α)
    (hx : R.Sat x) : R.Sat (Nat.iterate R.fix n x)
proof:
preserves_iterate R.Sat R.fix (fun y hy => by rw [R.absorbs y hy]; exact hy) n x hx

end IterateForm

end Lattice.Audit

name: Verdict
doc: **一次多段组合的判定**：逐段记录 `sequential` / `bridged`。
stmt: abbrev Verdict
proof: List CompositionKind

name: emptyVerdict
doc: **单位元**：空组合（无需任何转手）。
stmt: def emptyVerdict : Verdict

name: nil_append
stmt: theorem nil_append (ks : Verdict) : emptyVerdict ++ ks = ks
proof: List.nil_append ks

name: append_nil
stmt: theorem append_nil (ks : Verdict) : ks ++ emptyVerdict = ks
proof: List.append_nil ks

name: append_assoc
stmt: theorem append_assoc (a b c : Verdict) : (a ++ b) ++ c = a ++ (b ++ c)
proof: List.append_assoc a b c

name: bridgedCount
doc:
**需要多少座桥**：`bridged` 的个数。

`sequential` 不需要桥；`bridged` 需要一座。
stmt:
def bridgedCount : Verdict → ℕ
  | [] => 0
  | .sequential :: ks => bridgedCount ks
  | .bridged :: ks => bridgedCount ks + 1

name: bridgedCount_sequential
doc: **同性质不需要桥**。
stmt:
theorem bridgedCount_sequential (ks : Verdict) :
    bridgedCount (.sequential :: ks) = bridgedCount ks
proof: rfl

name: bridgedCount_bridged
doc: **换性质需要一座桥**。
stmt:
theorem bridgedCount_bridged (ks : Verdict) :
    bridgedCount (.bridged :: ks) = bridgedCount ks + 1
proof: rfl

name: bridgedCount_append
doc:
**同态**：拼接的桥数等于桥数之和。

⇒ **「需要多少桥」在判定层可计算，且与拼接相容。**
stmt:
theorem bridgedCount_append (a b : Verdict) :
    bridgedCount (a ++ b) = bridgedCount a + bridgedCount b
proof:
by
  induction a with
  | nil => simp [bridgedCount]
  | cons k ks ih =>
      cases k with
      | sequential => simp [bridgedCount, ih]
      | bridged => simp [bridgedCount, ih]; omega

name: bridgedCount_empty
doc: **空判定不需要桥**。
stmt: theorem bridgedCount_empty : bridgedCount emptyVerdict = 0
proof:
rfl

                     

                                                         

                  

                                           

           
         
                                                                                          
                                                         
                                                

                                        
instance : Monoid Verdict where
  mul := (· ++ ·)
  one := emptyVerdict
  mul_assoc := append_assoc
  one_mul := nil_append
  mul_one := append_nil

name: verdict_monoid
doc: **`Verdict` 构成 monoid**（三条律的显式陈述，保留以便审计逐条核对）。
stmt:
theorem verdict_monoid :
    (∀ ks : Verdict, emptyVerdict ++ ks = ks) ∧
    (∀ ks : Verdict, ks ++ emptyVerdict = ks) ∧
    (∀ a b c : Verdict, (a ++ b) ++ c = a ++ (b ++ c))
proof: ⟨nil_append, append_nil, append_assoc⟩

name: verdict_monoid_instance_agrees
doc:
**实例与显式陈述一致**：`Monoid` 的运算就是 `++`，单位就是 `emptyVerdict`。

⇒ 文档说的「monoid」现在指的是**注册的实例**，不是措辞。
stmt:
theorem verdict_monoid_instance_agrees :
    (∀ a b : Verdict, a * b = a ++ b) ∧ ((1 : Verdict) = emptyVerdict)
proof: ⟨fun _ _ => rfl, rfl⟩

name: bridgedCount_hom
doc: **`bridgedCount` 是 monoid 同态**：从 `(Verdict, ++, [])` 到 `(ℕ, +, 0)`。
stmt:
theorem bridgedCount_hom :
    bridgedCount emptyVerdict = 0 ∧
    (∀ a b : Verdict, bridgedCount (a ++ b) = bridgedCount a + bridgedCount b)
proof:
⟨bridgedCount_empty, bridgedCount_append⟩

end CompositionAlgebra

end Lattice.Audit

name: CompositionKind
doc: **一次组合属于哪一类。**
stmt:
inductive CompositionKind where
                        
  | sequential
                      
  | bridged
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: Evidence
doc:
**按判定结果需要提供的证据。**

`sequential` 是 `True`——**这说明它确实不需要额外东西**，而不是文档里那么一说。
`bridged` 是一条蕴含。
stmt:
def Evidence {α : Type} : CompositionKind → (α → Prop) → (α → Prop) → Prop
  | .sequential, _, _ => True
  | .bridged, P, Q => ∀ x, P x → Q x

name: Signature
doc:
**按判定结果决定的（证据类型，结论类型）对。**

这是本节的核心：**「需要什么」是一对类型，不是一个值。**
stmt: def Signature {α : Type} (k : CompositionKind) (P Q : α → Prop) : Prop × (α → Prop)
proof:
match k with
  | .sequential => (True, P)
  | .bridged => (∀ x, P x → Q x, Q)

name: compose_sequential
doc: **`sequential`：同性质，结论仍是该性质，无需任何额外证据。**
stmt:
theorem compose_sequential {α : Type} (P : α → Prop) (f g : α → α)
    (hf : ∀ x, P x → P (f x)) (hg : ∀ x, P x → P (g x))
    (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    P (g (f x))
proof: hg (f x) (hf x hx)

name: compose_bridged
doc: **`bridged`：换性质，结论是目标性质，代价是一条桥。**
stmt:
theorem compose_bridged {α : Type} (P Q : α → Prop) (f g : α → α)
    (hf : ∀ x, P x → P (f x)) (hg : ∀ x, Q x → Q (g x))
    (ev : Evidence .bridged P Q)
    (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    Q (g (f x))
proof: hg (f x) (ev (f x) (hf x hx))

name: signature_sequential
doc: **`sequential` 的签名**：证据 `True`，结论 `P`。
stmt:
theorem signature_sequential {α : Type} (P Q : α → Prop) :
    Signature .sequential P Q = (True, P)
proof: rfl

name: signature_bridged
doc: **`bridged` 的签名**：证据是桥，结论是 `Q`。
stmt:
theorem signature_bridged {α : Type} (P Q : α → Prop) :
    Signature .bridged P Q = (∀ x, P x → Q x, Q)
proof:
rfl

end CompositionClass

end Lattice.Audit

name: sq_le_needs_nonneg
doc:
**若无 `0 ≤ ε`，`r² ≤ ε² → |r| ≤ ε` 为假。**

反例 `r = 0, ε = -1`：`0 ≤ 1` 成立但 `|0| ≤ -1` 不成立。

这是 `ApproxExact.abs_le_of_sq_le` 那条前提的承重性证据。
stmt:
theorem sq_le_needs_nonneg :
    ¬ (∀ r ε : ℝ, r ^ 2 ≤ ε ^ 2 → |r| ≤ ε)
proof:
by
  intro h
  have hinst := h 0 (-1) (by norm_num)
  norm_num at hinst

name: eps_needs_nonneg
doc:
**同一反例也适用于 `epsSat_of_loss_le_sq` 的 `0 ≤ ε`。**

`EpsSat` 的定义含 `≤ ε`，所以负的 `ε` 会让它不可满足，
而 `loss ≤ ε²` 却可以被满足。
stmt:
theorem eps_needs_nonneg :
    ¬ (∀ ε : ℝ, (0 : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ ε ^ 2 → (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε)
proof:
by
  intro h
  have hinst := h (-1) (by norm_num)
  norm_num at hinst

name: lipschitz_needs_nonneg
doc:
**若无 `0 ≤ L`，Lipschitz 界 `d x s ≤ L * δ` 不能推出「`d x s ≤ 0`」。**

采样定理的核心一步是把 `d x s ≤ δ` 与 `|r x - r s| ≤ L * d x s` 相乘得到
`|r x - r s| ≤ L * δ`。若 `L < 0`，这个乘积是负数，
而 `|r x - r s|` 非负，于是界无法从假设导出。

反例：`L = -1`、`δ = 1`，则 `L * δ = -1 < 0 ≤ |r|`。
stmt:
theorem lipschitz_needs_nonneg :
    ¬ (∀ L δ : ℝ, 0 ≤ δ → (0 : ℝ) ≤ L * δ)
proof:
by
  intro h
  have hinst := h (-1) 1 (by norm_num)
  norm_num at hinst

name: delta_is_input
doc:
**`δ` 越大界越松**，所以 `δ` 不能省：它是界的**输入**，不是装饰。

这条说明采样密度在命题里是必需的：`δ = 0` 给出精确成立，
`δ > 0` 给出带界成立，两者不同。
stmt:
theorem delta_is_input :
    ¬ (∀ L δ : ℝ, 0 ≤ L → 0 ≤ δ → L * 0 = L * δ)
proof:
by
  intro h
  have hinst := h 1 1 (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
  norm_num at hinst

end Lattice.Audit

name: decreases_of_one_step
doc:
**若 `fix` 一步到目标且测度在目标为零，则 `decreases` 自动成立。**

设 `Sat` 是 `μ = 0` 的**精确**刻画（`∀ n, μ n = 0 ↔ Sat n`），
且 `fix` 一步就满足（`∀ n, Sat (fix n)`）。则对任何未满足的 `n`：

```
μ (fix n) = 0 < μ n
```

后者因为 `n` 未满足 ⟹ `μ n ≠ 0` ⟹ `μ n > 0`。

⇒ **在一步收敛的情形，`decreases` 是可导出的**，不是独立义务。
stmt:
theorem decreases_of_one_step {α : Type} (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) (μ : α → ℕ)
    (hzero : ∀ n, μ n = 0 ↔ Sat n) (hstep : ∀ n, Sat (fix n)) :
    ∀ n, ¬ Sat n → μ (fix n) < μ n
proof:
by
  intro n hn
  have hfix : μ (fix n) = 0 := (hzero (fix n)).mpr (hstep n)
  have hpos : 0 < μ n := by
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (μ n) with h | h
    · exact absurd ((hzero n).mp h) hn
    · exact h
  rw [hfix]
  exact hpos

name: decreases_role
doc:
**`decreases` 与「一步收敛」的关系**：
在一步收敛 + 原子性的场合，`decreases` 是**定理**而非**假设**。

这条与 `down_no_progress` 配对，完整刻画了 `decreases` 的角色：
它把「不收敛」排除掉，而当不收敛已被排除时它就被蕴含。
stmt:
theorem decreases_role {α : Type} (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) (μ : α → ℕ)
    (hzero : ∀ n, μ n = 0 ↔ Sat n) (hstep : ∀ n, Sat (fix n)) :
    (∀ n, ¬ Sat n → μ (fix n) < μ n) ∧ (∀ n, Sat (fix n))
proof:
⟨decreases_of_one_step Sat fix μ hzero hstep, hstep⟩

end Lattice.Audit

name: HypStatus
doc:
**一条前提的审计状态。**

「承重」与「结构必需」都必须附**理由**；「冗余」是唯一需要处置的状态。
stmt:
inductive HypStatus where
                        
  | loadBearing (counterexample : String)
                              
  | structurallyRequired (reason : String)
                       
  | redundant
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: IsRedundant
doc:
**冗余的判据**（不可自动判定，但可以陈述清楚）。

一条前提 `h` 对定理 `T` 冗余，当且仅当 `T` 的结论在**不含 `h`** 的前提下仍可证。
这是「命题在更弱假设下成立」，不是「命题被重新表述」。
stmt: def IsRedundant (provableWithout : Bool) : Prop
proof: provableWithout = true

name: chainAudit
doc:
证明链审计的结论。

每一条都指向证据（定理本身或反例），不是断言。
stmt: def chainAudit : List (String × HypStatus)
proof:
[ ("decodePayload_encodeForm : Inhabited R", .structurallyRequired
      "the instance is in decodePayload's signature; no statement mentioning it can omit it"),
    ("residual_le_of_zero_on_dense : 0 <= L", .loadBearing
      "machine-checked: Lattice.Audit.lipschitz_needs_nonneg shows a negative L makes the product bound false; rho is also 0 on the empty index set"),
    ("compileProgram_models : c mem ps", .loadBearing
      "without membership there is no link between c and the program"),
    ("compileProgram_sound : EntailsP ps x", .loadBearing
      "the conclusion is exactly the per-item obligation applied to membership"),
    ("converges_within : (R : Repair a)", .loadBearing
      "a generic statement needs the structure; dropping it leaves nothing to quantify over"),
    ("loss_eq_zero_of_poly_eq_zero : poly = 0", .loadBearing
      "loss is poly^2, so without the hypothesis the conclusion is false at poly = 1 (arithmetic witness: Lattice.Audit.sq_le_needs_nonneg)"),
    ("ladder_forward : satSym s", .loadBearing
      "l2l3_sound is exactly satSym -> satW, so the hypothesis is its antecedent"),
    ("abs_le_of_sq_le : 0 <= eps", .loadBearing
      "machine-checked counterexample: sq_le_needs_nonneg (r = 0, eps = -1)"),
    ("epsSat_of_loss_le_sq : 0 <= eps", .loadBearing
      "machine-checked counterexample: eps_needs_nonneg"),
    ("sampled bound : delta", .loadBearing
      "machine-checked: delta_is_input shows delta changes the bound") ]

name: no_redundant_hypotheses
doc:
**审计没有发现冗余前提。**

这是结论而非假设：`chainAudit` 中 `redundant` 的条目数为 0。
这条定理让「无冗余」可以被机器核对——若将来加入一条 `.redundant`，它会变成假。
stmt:
theorem no_redundant_hypotheses :
    (chainAudit.filter (fun p => p.2 == HypStatus.redundant)).length = 0
proof:
by
  decide

name: chainAudit_length
doc: 审计覆盖了七条定理。
stmt: theorem chainAudit_length : chainAudit.length = 10
proof: by decide

name: every_judgement_carries_a_reason
doc:
**每一条非冗余前提都附了理由**（反例或结构原因），没有空口断言。

`HypStatus` 的两个非冗余构造子都要求一个 `String` 理由，
所以这条性质是**类型保证**的，不需要证明——但值得陈述，
因为它是「审计不是走过场」的形式化。
stmt:
theorem every_judgement_carries_a_reason :
    ∀ p ∈ chainAudit, ∃ r : String,
      p.2 = HypStatus.loadBearing r ∨ p.2 = HypStatus.structurallyRequired r
proof:
by
  intro p hp
  obtain ⟨name, st⟩ := p
  cases st with
  | loadBearing r => exact ⟨r, Or.inl rfl⟩
  | structurallyRequired r => exact ⟨r, Or.inr rfl⟩
  | redundant =>
                                                                                        
    simp [chainAudit] at hp

end Lattice.Audit

name: Chain
doc:
**从性质 `P` 出发的组合链。**

`cons` 的 `rest` 项类型是 `Chain Q`，而 `Q` 正是 `h` 的**目标**——
⇒ **下一段的入口被强制等于这一段的出口**。`[change P Q, same R]`（`R ≠ Q`）构造不出来。
stmt:
inductive Chain (α : Type) : (α → Prop) → Type _ where
                 
  | nil (P : α → Prop) : Chain α P
                                        
  | cons {P : α → Prop} (Q : α → Prop) (h : ∀ x, P x → Q x) (rest : Chain α Q) :
      Chain α P

name: Chain.out
doc: **链的出口性质。**

name: Chain.length
stmt:
def Chain.length : {P : α → Prop} → Chain α P → ℕ
  | _, .nil _ => 0
  | _, .cons _ _ rest => rest.length + 1

name: compose_chain
doc:
**多段组合：`P x` ⟹ 链出口在 `x` 处成立。**

每一段用它自己的桥把性质送过去；`nil` 是恒等。
**这是第 59 轮两条两段定理的链形式。**
stmt:
theorem compose_chain : ∀ {P : α → Prop} (c : Chain α P) (x : α), P x → c.out x
  | _, .nil _, _, hx => hx
  | _, .cons _ h rest, x, hx => compose_chain rest x (h x hx)

name: chain_single
doc: **一段的链就是一次两段组合**（第 59 轮的 `compose_bridged`）。
stmt:
theorem chain_single {P Q : α → Prop} (h : ∀ x, P x → Q x) (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    (Chain.cons Q h (Chain.nil Q)).out x
proof: compose_chain (Chain.cons Q h (Chain.nil Q)) x hx

name: chain_two
stmt:
theorem chain_two {P Q R : α → Prop} (h1 : ∀ x, P x → Q x) (h2 : ∀ x, Q x → R x)
    (x : α) (hx : P x) :
    (Chain.cons Q h1 (Chain.cons R h2 (Chain.nil R))).out x
proof: compose_chain (Chain.cons Q h1 (Chain.cons R h2 (Chain.nil R))) x hx

name: out_determined_by_construction
doc:
**无法跳过中间性质**：链的出口由其构造子逐段决定。

若一个链的出口是 `R`，那么 `R` 必然是某一层的 `Q`，或空链的 `P`。
这条定理把「衔接由类型强制」写成一个可检查的事实：
**`out` 只依赖链的构造，不依赖任何外部声明。**
stmt:
theorem out_determined_by_construction {P R : α → Prop} (c : Chain α P) (h : c.out = R) :
    (c = Chain.nil P ∧ P = R) ∨
    (∃ (Q' : α → Prop) (hf : ∀ x, P x → Q' x) (rest : Chain α Q'),
        c = Chain.cons Q' hf rest ∧ rest.out = R)
proof:
by
  cases c with
  | nil P' =>
      left
      refine ⟨rfl, ?_⟩
      simpa [Chain.out] using h
  | cons Q hf rest =>
      right
      exact ⟨Q, hf, rest, rfl, h⟩

end MultiComposition

end Lattice.Audit

name: destructiveFix
doc:
**反例的修复步**：已满足点 `0` 被改成 `5`，其余点减一。

它故意不在 `Repair` 里出现——它缺 `absorbs`，正是本节要证明的。
stmt: def destructiveFix (n : ℕ) : ℕ
proof: if n = 0 then 5 else n - 1

name: destructiveFix_decreases
doc: 它在每个**未满足**点都严格下降。
stmt: theorem destructiveFix_decreases : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ (n = 0) → destructiveFix n < n
proof:
by
  intro n hn
  unfold destructiveFix
  rw [if_neg hn]
  omega

name: destructiveFix_atomic
doc: 它的测度只在目标为零，所以 `atomic` 成立。
stmt: theorem destructiveFix_atomic : ∀ n : ℕ, n = 0 → n = 0
proof: fun _ hn => hn

name: destructiveFix_not_absorbs
doc: **它违反吸收**：`0` 满足谓词，却被移走。
stmt: theorem destructiveFix_not_absorbs : ¬ (∀ n : ℕ, n = 0 → destructiveFix n = n)
proof:
by
  intro h
  have h0 := h 0 rfl
  unfold destructiveFix at h0
  norm_num at h0

name: absorbs_not_derivable
doc:
**`absorbs` 不可由另两条义务导出。**

量化形式：不存在一条「若 `decreases` 且 `atomic` 则 `absorbs`」的推导。

与 `Core/Repair.down_no_progress`（证 `atomic` 不可导出）配对，
两条合起来说明 `Repair` 的三条义务**没有一条是装饰**（`decreases` 除外，
见文件头 §4 记录的缺口）。
stmt:
theorem absorbs_not_derivable :
    ¬ (∀ (Sat : ℕ → Prop) (fix : ℕ → ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℕ),
        (∀ n, ¬ Sat n → μ (fix n) < μ n) →
        (∀ n, μ n = 0 → Sat n) →
        ∀ n, Sat n → fix n = n)
proof:
by
  intro h
  have h' : ∀ n : ℕ, n = 0 → destructiveFix n = n :=
    h (fun n => n = 0) destructiveFix (fun n => n)
      destructiveFix_decreases destructiveFix_atomic
  exact destructiveFix_not_absorbs h'

name: ascendingFix
doc:
**上升算子**：非零点加一，零点固定。

它吸收、原子，**不下降**。
stmt: def ascendingFix (n : ℕ) : ℕ
proof: if n = 0 then 0 else n + 1

name: ascendingFix_absorbs
doc: 它吸收。
stmt: theorem ascendingFix_absorbs : ∀ n : ℕ, n = 0 → ascendingFix n = n
proof:
by
  intro n hn; subst hn; rfl

name: ascendingFix_atomic
doc: 它是原子的（度量取 `id`）。
stmt: theorem ascendingFix_atomic : ∀ n : ℕ, n = 0 → n = 0
proof: fun _ hn => hn

name: ascendingFix_not_decreases
doc: **它不下降**：`n = 5` 时 `ascendingFix 5 = 6 > 5`。
stmt:
theorem ascendingFix_not_decreases :
    ¬ (∀ n : ℕ, ¬ (n = 0) → ascendingFix n < n)
proof:
by
  intro h
  have h5 := h 5 (by decide)
  unfold ascendingFix at h5
  simp at h5

name: decreases_not_derivable
doc:
**`decreases` 不可导出**：存在一个算子满足 `absorbs` 与 `atomic`，却违反 `decreases`。

**这是三块独立性证明的最后一块**（另两块是 `down_no_progress` 与 `destructiveFix`）。
stmt:
theorem decreases_not_derivable :
    ∃ fix : ℕ → ℕ,
      (∀ n : ℕ, n = 0 → fix n = n) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, (fun k => k) n = 0 → n = 0) ∧
      ¬ (∀ n : ℕ, ¬ (n = 0) → (fun k => k) (fix n) < (fun k => k) n)
proof:
⟨ascendingFix, ascendingFix_absorbs, ascendingFix_atomic, ascendingFix_not_decreases⟩

end Lattice.Audit

name: isRedundant_true
doc:
**`IsRedundant` 非空**：`provableWithout = true` 时它成立。

这是它最直接的模型——「不需要额外前提即可证」，正是名字的意思。
stmt: theorem isRedundant_true : IsRedundant true
proof: rfl

name: commutativeBlock_trivial
doc:
**`CommutativeBlock` 非空**：恒真关系在任意 `n` 上对称。

取恒真关系是这个谓词最退化的模型；它证明 `CommutativeBlock` 对任意 `n` 都有实例，
所以定义不是空集。非退化的对称关系属 `RealEffectOrdering` 的主题内容。
stmt:
theorem commutativeBlock_trivial (n : ℕ) :
    Lattice.Lib.Compiler.RealEffectOrdering.CommutativeBlock (n := n) (fun _ _ => True)
proof: fun _ _ _ => trivial

name: isPolicyDensity_const_one
doc:
**`IsPolicyDensity` 非空**：概率测度上的常函数 `1` 是策略密度。

两项各自成立：`1 ≥ 0` 处处（故几乎处处），且 `∫ 1 ∂μ = μ univ = 1`。

**注意 `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]` 不是回避**：`IsPolicyDensity` 的定义就要求 `∫ π ∂μ = 1`，
所以非概率测度上它必然没有实例。这个见证说明的是「该谓词在它该有实例的地方有实例」。
stmt:
theorem isPolicyDensity_const_one {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α)
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : IsPolicyDensity μ (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
proof:
by
  constructor
  · filter_upwards with a
    norm_num
  · simp

name: keyOrthogonal_zero
doc:
**`KeyOrthogonal` 非空**：键为零向量的行与任何行正交。

`inner p.k 0 = 0`，所以 `KeyOrthogonal p ⟨·, 0⟩` 对任意 `p` 成立。
stmt:
theorem keyOrthogonal_zero {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (p : RowVec E) : KeyOrthogonal p ⟨0, 0⟩
proof:
by
  unfold KeyOrthogonal
  simp

name: isometryScalar_id
doc:
**`IsometryScalar` 非空**：恒等映射保内积。

`⟪id q, id k⟫ = ⟪q, k⟫` 是 `rfl`。这条见证把「等距」这个谓词与最基本的等距映射连起来。
stmt:
theorem isometryScalar_id {𝕜 E : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] :
    Lattice.IsometryScalar (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (id : E → E)
proof:
fun _ _ => rfl

                     

                                                                   
                                       
  
                                           
                                                

end Lattice.Audit

name: FieldRole
doc:
**一条字段在结构中的角色。**

「义务」是待证明的断言；「数据」是被其他字段引用的对象。
区别在于：删掉数据，结构无法陈说；删掉义务，结构**能陈说但不再承诺**。
stmt:
inductive FieldRole where
                              
  | obligation
                               
  | datum
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: StructureCensus
doc: **一个结构的字段清册。**
stmt:
structure StructureCensus where
             
  name : String
              
  fields : ℕ
               
  obligations : ℕ
                                               
  nestedObligations : ℕ
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: census
doc: **四个结构 + `Tokenizer` 的实测清册。**
stmt: def census : List StructureCensus
proof:
[ { name := "Compiler", fields := 5, obligations := 1, nestedObligations := 0 },
    { name := "Representation", fields := 8, obligations := 1, nestedObligations := 0 },
    { name := "Ladder", fields := 6, obligations := 1, nestedObligations := 2 },
    { name := "Tokenizer", fields := 3, obligations := 1, nestedObligations := 0 },
    { name := "Repair", fields := 6, obligations := 3, nestedObligations := 0 } ]

name: census_length
doc: 清册长度。
stmt: theorem census_length : census.length = 5
proof: by decide

name: repair_is_densest
doc: **`Repair` 是义务密度最高的结构**：3/6 = 50%，其余都 ≤ 33%。
stmt:
theorem repair_is_densest :
    (census.filter (fun s => s.obligations * 2 ≥ s.fields)).length = 1
proof: by decide

name: total_obligations
doc:
**所有结构的义务总数**（含嵌套）：9 条。

`Compiler` 1 + `Representation` 1 + `Ladder` 1+2 + `Tokenizer` 1 + `Repair` 3 = 9。
stmt:
theorem total_obligations :
    (census.map (fun s => s.obligations + s.nestedObligations)).sum = 9
proof: by decide

name: no_zero_obligation_structure
doc:
**没有结构是零义务的**：每个结构都至少承诺一件事。

这条排除了「结构只是数据容器」的可能——库里的每个结构都有实质义务。
stmt:
theorem no_zero_obligation_structure :
    ∀ s ∈ census, s.obligations ≥ 1
proof:
by
  intro s hs
  simp [census] at hs
  rcases hs with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> decide

end Lattice.Audit

name: kindToBool
doc: `sequential ↦ false`（无需额外证据），`bridged ↦ true`（需要一条蕴含）。
stmt:
def kindToBool : CompositionKind → Bool
  | .sequential => false
  | .bridged => true

name: boolToKind
doc: `Bool` 回到判定。
stmt:
def boolToKind : Bool → CompositionKind
  | false => .sequential
  | true => .bridged

name: kindToBool_boolToKind
stmt: theorem kindToBool_boolToKind (b : Bool) : kindToBool (boolToKind b) = b
proof:
by
  cases b <;> rfl

name: boolToKind_kindToBool
stmt: theorem boolToKind_kindToBool (k : CompositionKind) : boolToKind (kindToBool k) = k
proof:
by
  cases k <;> rfl

name: kindLe
doc:
**判定强度的序**：`a ≤ b` 当且仅当 `b` 需要的证据不少于 `a`。

按 `Bool` 编码，`false < true`，即 `sequential < bridged`。**这是「需求更弱」的方向**：
`sequential` 是底（什么都不要），`bridged` 是顶（要一条蕴含）。
stmt: def kindLe (a b : CompositionKind) : Prop
proof: kindToBool a ≤ kindToBool b

name: kindLe_iff
doc:
**序的显式形式**：`a ≤ b` 当且仅当 `a` 是 `sequential` 或者 `b` 是 `bridged`。

这条把「一段蕴含的两种极端」写成了序关系，比 `Bool` 编码更直接从 `Evidence` 的定义读出来。
stmt: theorem kindLe_iff (a b : CompositionKind) : kindLe a b ↔ a = .sequential ∨ b = .bridged
proof:
by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [kindLe, kindToBool]

name: kindLe_refl
stmt: theorem kindLe_refl (a : CompositionKind) : kindLe a a
proof:
by
  cases a <;> simp [kindLe, kindToBool]

name: kindLe_antisymm
stmt: theorem kindLe_antisymm {a b : CompositionKind} (h₁ : kindLe a b) (h₂ : kindLe b a) : a = b
proof:
by
  have hb : ∀ x y : Bool, x ≤ y → y ≤ x → x = y := by decide
  have h : kindToBool a = kindToBool b := hb _ _ h₁ h₂
  calc a = boolToKind (kindToBool a) := (boolToKind_kindToBool a).symm
    _ = boolToKind (kindToBool b) := by rw [h]
    _ = b := boolToKind_kindToBool b

name: kindLe_trans
stmt:
theorem kindLe_trans {a b c : CompositionKind} (h₁ : kindLe a b) (h₂ : kindLe b c) :
    kindLe a c
proof:
by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> simp_all [kindLe, kindToBool]

name: kindLe_bot
doc: **底**：`sequential` 满足任何要求的下界。
stmt: theorem kindLe_bot (a : CompositionKind) : kindLe .sequential a
proof:
by
  rw [kindLe_iff]; exact Or.inl rfl

name: kindLe_top
doc: **顶**：`bridged` 是一切的上界。
stmt: theorem kindLe_top (a : CompositionKind) : kindLe a .bridged
proof:
by
  rw [kindLe_iff]; exact Or.inr rfl

name: kindSup
doc: **并**：任取一个仍是上界的最小者。在 `CompositionKind` 上就是 `bridged`（除非两者都弱）。
stmt: def kindSup (a b : CompositionKind) : CompositionKind
proof: if kindToBool a then .bridged else b

name: kindInf
doc: **交**：取较弱的那个。
stmt: def kindInf (a b : CompositionKind) : CompositionKind
proof: if kindToBool a then b else .sequential

name: kindLe_sup_left
stmt: theorem kindLe_sup_left (a b : CompositionKind) : kindLe a (kindSup a b)
proof:
by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [kindLe, kindToBool, kindSup]

name: kindLe_sup_right
stmt: theorem kindLe_sup_right (a b : CompositionKind) : kindLe b (kindSup a b)
proof:
by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [kindLe, kindToBool, kindSup]

name: kindSup_le
stmt:
theorem kindSup_le {a b c : CompositionKind} (h₁ : kindLe a c) (h₂ : kindLe b c) :
    kindLe (kindSup a b) c
proof:
by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [kindLe, kindToBool, kindSup]

name: kindInf_le_left
stmt: theorem kindInf_le_left (a b : CompositionKind) : kindLe (kindInf a b) a
proof:
by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [kindLe, kindToBool, kindInf]

name: kindInf_le_right
stmt: theorem kindInf_le_right (a b : CompositionKind) : kindLe (kindInf a b) b
proof:
by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp [kindLe, kindToBool, kindInf]

name: kindLe_inf
stmt:
theorem kindLe_inf {a b c : CompositionKind} (h₁ : kindLe c a) (h₂ : kindLe c b) :
    kindLe c (kindInf a b)
proof:
by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [kindLe, kindToBool, kindInf]

name: kind_is_bounded_lattice
doc:
**`CompositionKind` 的判定代数是一个有界格。**

`kindLe_*` + `kindSup_le` / `kindLe_sup_left` / `kindLe_sup_right` 给出上确界，
`kindInf_*` 给出下确界，`kindLe_bot` / `kindLe_top` 给出界。
stmt:
theorem kind_is_bounded_lattice :
    (∀ a, kindLe a a) ∧ (∀ a b c, kindLe a b → kindLe b c → kindLe a c) ∧
    (∀ a, kindLe .sequential a) ∧ (∀ a, kindLe a .bridged) ∧
    (∀ a b, kindLe a (kindSup a b) ∧ kindLe b (kindSup a b) ∧
      ∀ c, kindLe a c → kindLe b c → kindLe (kindSup a b) c)
proof:
⟨kindLe_refl, fun _ _ _ => kindLe_trans,
   kindLe_bot, kindLe_top,
   fun a b => ⟨kindLe_sup_left a b, kindLe_sup_right a b, fun c h₁ h₂ => kindSup_le h₁ h₂⟩⟩

name: verdictLe
doc: **`Verdict` 的逐点序**：逐段比较强度，长度必须相同。
stmt: def verdictLe : List CompositionKind → List CompositionKind → Prop
proof: List.Forall₂ kindLe

name: verdict_no_sup
doc:
**`Verdict` 不是格。**

反例是长度不同的两个判定：

```lean
[.bridged]                   -- 1 段
[.sequential, .sequential]   -- 2 段
```

`Forall₂` 强制上界与两个下界**等长**，所以上界长度必须同时是 1 与 2——矛盾。
**这就是本库的组合代数天然是 monoid 而不是格的原因**：组合是拼接，而拼接不保持长度。
stmt:
theorem verdict_no_sup :
    ¬ ∃ u : List CompositionKind,
        verdictLe [.bridged] u ∧ verdictLe [.sequential, .sequential] u
proof:
by
  rintro ⟨u, h₁, h₂⟩
  have len₁ : u.length = 1 := by
    simpa using (List.Forall₂.length_eq h₁).symm
  have len₂ : u.length = 2 := by
    simpa using (List.Forall₂.length_eq h₂).symm
  omega

name: verdict_lub_of_length_eq
doc:
**定长化之后它确实是格**：长度相同的两个判定有逐点上界（取逐段的 `kindSup`）。

这不是空话——它是「`Verdict` 为什么只是 monoid」这个问题的正面回答：**格结构被长度破坏，
而长度相同的切片上格结构仍在。**
stmt:
theorem verdict_lub_of_length_eq {a b : List CompositionKind} (h : a.length = b.length) :
    ∃ u : List CompositionKind, u.length = a.length ∧ verdictLe a u ∧ verdictLe b u
proof:
by
  induction a generalizing b with
  | nil =>
      cases b with
      | nil => exact ⟨[], rfl, .nil, .nil⟩
      | cons _ _ => simp at h
  | cons x xs ih =>
      cases b with
      | nil => simp at h
      | cons y ys =>
          simp only [List.length_cons, Nat.add_right_cancel_iff] at h
          obtain ⟨u, hu_len, hu_a, hu_b⟩ := ih h
          exact ⟨kindSup x y :: u, by simp [hu_len],
                 List.Forall₂.cons (kindLe_sup_left x y) hu_a,
                 List.Forall₂.cons (kindLe_sup_right x y) hu_b⟩

name: lattice_holds_per_segment_not_per_sequence
doc:
**结论**：库名里的「格」在**每段判定**上成立，在**判定序列**上不成立。

这一条不是措辞妥协，是两条定理的合取：`kind_is_bounded_lattice` 与 `verdict_no_sup`。
stmt:
theorem lattice_holds_per_segment_not_per_sequence :
    (∀ a : CompositionKind, kindLe .sequential a ∧ kindLe a .bridged) ∧
    (¬ ∃ u : List CompositionKind,
        verdictLe [.bridged] u ∧ verdictLe [.sequential, .sequential] u)
proof:
⟨fun a => ⟨kindLe_bot a, kindLe_top a⟩, verdict_no_sup⟩

end Lattice.Audit

name: StackLayer
doc:
**网络栈的一层**：仿射映射，可带激活。

`act` 是 `Option (ℝ → ℝ)`：`none` 表示纯仿射，`some σ` 表示该层之后施加 `σ`。
stmt:
structure StackLayer (n : ℕ) where
              
  affine : AffineLayer (Fin n)
                 
  act : Option (ℝ → ℝ)

name: layerApply
doc: **一层的作用**：先仿射，再（若有）逐坐标施加激活。
stmt: noncomputable def layerApply (L : StackLayer n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ
proof:
match L.act with
  | none => affineAct L.affine x
  | some σ => fun j => σ (affineAct L.affine x j)

name: actStackEval
doc: **整条栈的求值**：从左到右 foldl。
stmt: noncomputable def actStackEval (ls : List (StackLayer n)) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ
proof: ls.foldl (fun acc L => layerApply L acc) x

name: actStackEval_nil
doc: **空栈是恒等**。
stmt: @[simp] theorem actStackEval_nil (x : Fin n → ℝ) : actStackEval [] x = x
proof: rfl

name: actStackSingle_affine
doc: **单个纯仿射层就是仿射映射**：`act = none` 时 `layerApply` 退化为 `affineAct`。
stmt:
theorem actStackSingle_affine (p : AffineLayer (Fin n)) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    layerApply ⟨p, none⟩ x = affineAct p x
proof: rfl

name: actStackEval_of_no_activation
doc:
**纯仿射栈就是 `netAct`**：所有层的 `act` 都是 `none` 时，两种求值一致。

⇒ **多层的纯仿射栈不增加表达力**，这是 §1.3 的前半部分。
stmt:
theorem actStackEval_of_no_activation (ps : List (AffineLayer (Fin n))) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    actStackEval (ps.map fun p => ⟨p, none⟩) x = netAct ps x
proof:
by
  induction ps generalizing x with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons p ps ih =>
      show actStackEval ((⟨p, none⟩ :: ps.map fun q => ⟨q, none⟩)) x = netAct (p :: ps) x
      show actStackEval (ps.map fun q => ⟨q, none⟩) (layerApply ⟨p, none⟩ x) =
        netAct ps (affineAct p x)
      rw [ih]
      rfl

name: relu_key_values
stmt: theorem relu_key_values : relu 0 = 0 ∧ relu 1 = 1 ∧ relu (-1) = 0
proof:
by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp only [relu] <;> norm_num

name: relu_not_affine
doc:
**`relu` 不是任何仿射函数**：不存在 `a b : ℝ` 使 `∀ x, relu x = a * x + b`。

**证明**：假设有。由 `x = 0` 得 `b = 0`，由 `x = 1` 得 `a = 1`，
于是 `x = -1` 处右边是 `-1`，但 `relu (-1) = 0`。矛盾。

⇒ **这一条就是「激活让栈超出仿射类」的**最小见证。
stmt: theorem relu_not_affine : ¬ ∃ (a b : ℝ), ∀ x : ℝ, relu x = a * x + b
proof:
by
  rintro ⟨a, b, h⟩
  have h0 : b = 0 := by
    have := h 0
    simp only [relu, max_eq_left (le_refl (0 : ℝ)), mul_zero, zero_add] at this
    exact this.symm
  have h1 : a = 1 := by
    have := h 1
    rw [h0] at this
    simp only [relu, max_eq_left (zero_le_one' ℝ), mul_one, add_zero] at this
    exact this.symm
  have hm : relu (-1) = 0 := relu_key_values.2.2
  have := h (-1)
  rw [h1, h0] at this
  simp only [mul_neg, mul_one, zero_add] at this
  rw [hm] at this
  norm_num at this

name: activation_strictly_stronger
doc:
**带激活的栈严格强于纯仿射栈。**

两个方向：

1. **纯仿射栈能做的，激活栈都能做**（`actStackEval_of_no_activation`）；
2. **激活栈能做的，纯仿射栈不都能做**（`relu_not_affine`）。

⇒ **第 135 轮 `MultiLayerLadder` 里「多层」这个词，在纯仿射的设置下确实没有实际内容；
加入激活之后它才有。** 这条定理把这个区别显式地记录了下来。
stmt:
theorem activation_strictly_stronger :
    (∀ (ps : List (AffineLayer (Fin n))) (x : Fin n → ℝ),
        actStackEval (ps.map fun p => ⟨p, none⟩) x = netAct ps x) ∧
    (¬ ∃ (a b : ℝ), ∀ x : ℝ, relu x = a * x + b)
proof:
⟨actStackEval_of_no_activation, relu_not_affine⟩

end Activation

end Lattice.Core

name: twoVar
doc: A two-variable form.
stmt: def twoVar : LinearForm Int 2

name: noVar
doc: A zero-variable point, which the legacy `dot` accepted for `twoVar`.
stmt: def noVar : Point Int 0
proof:
fun i => i.elim0

                                                                        
                                                         
  
                                                                                  
                                                                                      
#check_failure (twoVar.denote noVar)

                                                              

                                                               
example : twoVar.denote (fun i => if i = 0 then 1 else 0) = 3 := by
  simp [twoVar, LinearForm.denote, Fin.sum_univ_two]

                                                           

section Linearity

variable {R : Type} [CommSemiring R] {n : Nat}

name: denote_zero
doc: Denotation of the zero form is zero.
stmt:
theorem denote_zero (x : Point R n) :
    (⟨fun _ => 0, 0⟩ : LinearForm R n).denote x = 0
proof:
by
  simp [LinearForm.denote]

name: denote_neg_core
doc: Denotation of a sum of coefficient vectors is the sum of denotations.
stmt:
theorem denote_neg_core (c d : LinearForm R n) (x : Point R n) :
    (⟨fun i => c.a i + d.a i, c.b + d.b⟩ : LinearForm R n).denote x
      = c.denote x + d.denote x
proof:
by
  simp only [LinearForm.denote, Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_mul]
  ring

end Linearity

                                                            

                                                                                    
                                           

section Behaviour

variable {Param : Type} [WeightSemantics Param]

name: be_refl
stmt: theorem be_refl (p : Param) : BehaviourallyEquivalent p p
proof: fun _ => rfl

name: be_symm
stmt:
theorem be_symm {p q : Param} (h : BehaviourallyEquivalent p q) :
    BehaviourallyEquivalent q p
proof: fun x => (h x).symm

name: be_trans
proof:
fun x => (hpq x).trans (hqr x)

end Behaviour

end Lattice.Core.Check

name: IdempotentOn
doc: **An operator that is the identity on a subset.** `S` selects the subset; `g` is the operator.
stmt: def IdempotentOn {α : Type} (S : α → Prop) (g : α → α) : Prop
proof: ∀ x, S x → g x = x

name: IdempotentOn.iterate
doc:
**Iterating preserves idempotence on the same subset.**

The induction uses the hypothesis twice: once at `x` (to collapse the last step) and once at the already-fixed
intermediate value. Both applications need `S` to be preserved by `g`, which is why the hypothesis is stated for
*all* elements of `S` rather than for `x` alone.
proof:
by
  intro x hx
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, h x hx]

name: idempotentOn_of_leftInverse
doc:
**A left inverse makes the composite idempotent everywhere.**

`extract ∘ compile` is the identity on the whole space whenever `extract` is a left inverse of `compile`; this is
the round-trip side's instance, stated without reference to any particular representation.
stmt:
theorem idempotentOn_of_leftInverse {P W : Type} (compile : P → W) (extract : W → P)
    (hround : ∀ p, extract (compile p) = p) :
    IdempotentOn (fun _ => True) (extract ∘ compile)
proof: fun p _ => hround p

name: iterate_comp_of_leftInverse
doc: **… and so is every iterate of it.**
stmt:
theorem iterate_comp_of_leftInverse {P W : Type} (compile : P → W) (extract : W → P)
    (hround : ∀ p, extract (compile p) = p) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ p : P, (extract ∘ compile)^[n] p = p
proof:
fun p => IdempotentOn.iterate (idempotentOn_of_leftInverse compile extract hround) n p trivial

end Lattice.Core

name: Preserves
doc:
**A repair preserves a predicate** when it does not move a satisfied state out of the predicate.

Only meaningful as an obligation at satisfying states: at an unsatisfying state the repair *must* move, so no
predicate containing that state can be preserved by an operator that reaches its target. `preserves_free`
below records that the distinction is real.
stmt: def Preserves (P : α → Prop) (R : Repair α) : Prop
proof: ∀ x : α, P x → P (R.fix x)

name: preserves_of_sat
doc:
**At a satisfying state the repair preserves everything.**

`Repair.absorbs` says `fix` is the identity there, so any predicate is preserved -- not by analysing the
predicate, but because nothing changes. This is the layered statement the geometry's third quality level rests
on: conservativity implies preservation of every invariant at once.
stmt:
theorem preserves_of_sat (R : Repair α) (P : α → Prop) (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) :
    P x → P (R.fix x)
proof:
by
  rw [R.absorbs x h]
  exact id

name: fix_eq_self_of_sat
doc: **A satisfied state is a fixed point**, which is the fact `preserves_of_sat` uses.
stmt: theorem fix_eq_self_of_sat (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) : R.fix x = x
proof: R.absorbs x h

name: preserves_free
doc:
**Preservation is not free at unsatisfying states.**

For any unsatisfying state there is a predicate it satisfies that the repair cannot preserve -- namely "being
this state". So the obligation is only meaningful as a conditional, and a framework that demanded
unconditional preservation would have no inhabitants at all.
stmt:
theorem preserves_free (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : ¬ R.Sat x) :
    ∃ P : α → Prop, P x ∧ ¬ P (R.fix x)
proof:
by
  refine ⟨fun y => y = x, rfl, ?_⟩
  intro hfix
  have hdec := R.decreases x h
  rw [hfix] at hdec
  exact absurd hdec (lt_irrefl _)

name: Compatible
doc:
**A predicate and a target are compatible** when some state satisfies both.

An earlier revision of this file claimed this separates a *good* repair from a merely correct one. It does
not, and the correction is worth recording.

`Compatible P R` asks whether the **target** can be met without leaving `P`. It says nothing about how `R`
gets there: two operators with the same `Sat` have the same `Compatible` verdict whatever their `fix` does.
And when `P` is *inconsistent* with the target -- separation versus a coincidence constraint, say -- no
operator can satisfy it, so the failure is a property of the pair (constraint, predicate) rather than a
weakness of the operator.

So this is an obligation on the **constraint**, checked against a predicate, and it is stated with `R` only
because a `Repair` is where a constraint lives in this project. `compatible_iff_witness` below gives its
content: it is nonemptiness of the intersection.
stmt: def Compatible (P : α → Prop) (R : Repair α) : Prop
proof: ∀ x : α, P x → ∃ y : α, R.Sat y ∧ P y

name: compatible_iff_witness
doc:
**What `Compatible` actually asserts** (given a `P`-satisfying state to start from): the target and the
predicate have a common point.

Every `x` with `P x` yields the same witness obligation, so the `∀ x` is not doing any work beyond saying
that `P` is inhabited.
stmt:
theorem compatible_iff_witness (P : α → Prop) (R : Repair α) (x₀ : α) (hx₀ : P x₀) :
    Compatible P R ↔ ∃ y : α, R.Sat y ∧ P y
proof:
by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact h x₀ hx₀
  · intro ⟨y, hsat, hP⟩ _ _
    exact ⟨y, hsat, hP⟩

end Lattice.Core

name: SatisfiesEq
doc: A point satisfies an equality constraint when the linear form vanishes there.
stmt: def SatisfiesEq (c : LinearForm R n) (x : Point R n) : Prop
proof: c.denote x = 0

name: SatisfiesLe
doc: A point satisfies a `≤` constraint when the linear form is non-positive there.
stmt: def SatisfiesLe (c : LinearForm R n) (x : Point R n) : Prop
proof: c.denote x ≤ 0

name: SatisfiesLt
doc: A point satisfies a `<` constraint when the linear form is negative there.
stmt: def SatisfiesLt (c : LinearForm R n) (x : Point R n) : Prop
proof: c.denote x < 0

name: Satisfies
doc: Satisfaction for the unified constraint syntax.
stmt: def Satisfies (c : Constraint R n) (x : Point R n) : Prop
proof:
match c.rel with
  | .eq => SatisfiesEq c.form x
  | .le => SatisfiesLe c.form x
  | .lt => SatisfiesLt c.form x

name: Entails
doc:
A point satisfies a *set* of constraints when it satisfies every one of them.

This is the program-level notion the bridge theorems quantify over.
stmt: def Entails (cs : List (Constraint R n)) (x : Point R n) : Prop
proof: ∀ c ∈ cs, Satisfies c x

name: Models
doc:
`H` models `c`: every point meeting every constraint in `H` also meets `c`.

This is *deliberately* stronger than `Entails`, and it is the correct target for a
"the compiled artifact preserves the meaning of the program" claim.
stmt: def Models (H : List (Constraint R n)) (c : Constraint R n) : Prop
proof:
∀ x : Point R n, Entails H x → Satisfies c x

end Satisfaction

                             

                                                                                  

section Structural

variable {R : Type} [CommSemiring R] [LinearOrder R] {n : Nat}

name: entails_cons
doc: Entailment of a cons is entailment of the head together with entailment of the tail.
stmt:
theorem entails_cons {c : Constraint R n} {cs : List (Constraint R n)} {x : Point R n} :
    Entails (c :: cs) x ↔ Satisfies c x ∧ Entails cs x
proof:
by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨h c (List.mem_cons_self _ _),
      fun d hd => h d (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hd)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hc, hcs⟩ d hd
    rcases List.mem_cons.mp hd with rfl | hd'
    · exact hc
    · exact hcs d hd'

name: entails_mono
doc:
Entailment is monotone in the constraint set: a superset entails at least as much.

This is the statement that a *larger* symbolic program is *stronger*, which the
embedding direction of the bridge relies on.
stmt:
theorem entails_mono {cs ds : List (Constraint R n)} {x : Point R n}
    (hsub : ∀ c ∈ cs, c ∈ ds) (h : Entails ds x) : Entails cs x
proof: fun c hc => h c (hsub c hc)

name: models_of_mem
doc: A single constraint is entailed by any set containing it.
stmt:
theorem models_of_mem {H : List (Constraint R n)} {c : Constraint R n}
    (hmem : c ∈ H) : Models H c
proof: fun _x hx => hx c hmem

name: models_of_subset
doc:
Models is monotone (contravariantly) in the hypothesis set.

`models_of_subset` reads: if `H ⊆ K` (every hypothesis of `H` is also one of `K`),
then anything modelled by `H` is modelled by `K`. A point satisfying the larger set
`K` certainly satisfies the smaller one `H`.
stmt:
theorem models_of_subset {H K : List (Constraint R n)} {c : Constraint R n}
    (hsub : ∀ d ∈ H, d ∈ K) (h : Models H c) : Models K c
proof:
fun x hx => h x (entails_mono (cs := H) (ds := K) hsub hx)

end Structural

end Lattice.Core

name: AffineLayer
doc: An affine layer over a fixed width: weights and a bias on `n → ℝ`.
stmt:
structure AffineLayer (n : Type) where
                       
  W : n → n → ℝ
                     
  b : n → ℝ

name: affineAct
doc: The action of one affine layer.
stmt: noncomputable def affineAct {n : Type} [Fintype n] (p : AffineLayer n) (x : n → ℝ) : n → ℝ
proof: fun j => (∑ i, p.W i j * x i) + p.b j

name: netAct
doc:
A stack of same-width affine layers, applied left to right.

Defined by `List.foldl` so that the empty stack is the identity and appending stacks composes them
in order -- the two facts `netAct_nil` and `netAct_append` record.
stmt:
noncomputable def netAct {n : Type} [Fintype n] (ls : List (AffineLayer n)) (x : n → ℝ) :
    n → ℝ
proof: ls.foldl (fun acc p => affineAct p acc) x

name: netAct_nil
doc: The empty stack is the identity.
stmt:
@[simp] theorem netAct_nil {n : Type} [Fintype n] (x : n → ℝ) :
    netAct ([] : List (AffineLayer n)) x = x
proof: rfl

name: netAct_append
doc:
**Composition law.** A stack of two stacks is the second applied to the first.

This is what lets a multi-layer network be reasoned about as a single map, and it is the form the
ladder needs if a stack is to be treated as one rung.
stmt:
theorem netAct_append {n : Type} [Fintype n] (ls ms : List (AffineLayer n)) (x : n → ℝ) :
    netAct (ls ++ ms) x = netAct ms (netAct ls x)
proof:
by
  unfold netAct
  rw [List.foldl_append]

name: relu
doc: The rectifier, as a function on the reals.
stmt: def relu (x : ℝ) : ℝ
proof: max x 0

name: relu_not_injective
doc: `relu` is not injective: both `-1` and `0` map to `0`.
stmt: theorem relu_not_injective : ¬ Function.Injective relu
proof:
by
  intro h
  have hz : relu (-1) = relu 0 := by
    simp only [relu]
    norm_num
  have : (-1 : ℝ) = 0 := h hz
  norm_num at this

name: reluVec
doc: Componentwise rectification of a vector.
stmt: noncomputable def reluVec {n : Type} (x : n → ℝ) : n → ℝ
proof: fun j => relu (x j)

name: netRelu_not_injective
doc:
**A stack followed by an activation is not injective.**

`n := Fin 1` suffices: the two inputs that differ only in sign are both mapped to `0` by `relu`,
regardless of the stack, so the whole map collapses them.
stmt:
theorem netRelu_not_injective :
    ¬ Function.Injective (fun x : Fin 1 → ℝ => reluVec (netAct [] x))
proof:
by
  intro h
                                          
  have hsame : reluVec (netAct ([] : List (AffineLayer (Fin 1))) (fun _ => (-1 : ℝ)))
      = reluVec (netAct ([] : List (AffineLayer (Fin 1))) (fun _ => (0 : ℝ))) := by
    funext j
    simp only [reluVec, netAct, List.foldl_nil, relu]
    norm_num
  have hinj := h hsame
  have : (fun _ : Fin 1 => (-1 : ℝ)) = (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)) := hinj
  have := congrFun this ⟨0, by decide⟩
  norm_num at this

name: reversibility_spectrum
doc:
**Reversibility depends on the representation and the structure.**

* `LinearForm`: not injective -- `Lattice.Lift.Extraction` exhibits two distinct coefficient vectors
  with the same zero set.
* One affine layer: injective -- `Lattice.Core.Weight.layer_act_injective`.
* A stack with a rectifier: not injective -- `netRelu_not_injective`.

The middle conjunct is what makes the spectrum non-trivial: a single affine layer *is* invertible,
so "the semantic layer is not invertible" is false as a blanket statement about weights.
stmt:
theorem reversibility_spectrum :
                                    
    (∀ {m n : Type} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] {p q : LayerParams m n},
        BehaviourallyEquivalent p q → p = q)
                                              
    ∧ ¬ Function.Injective (fun x : Fin 1 → ℝ => reluVec (netAct [] x))
                                      
    ∧ ¬ Function.Injective relu
proof:
⟨fun {_ _ _ _ _ _} => layer_act_injective, netRelu_not_injective, relu_not_injective⟩

end Lattice.Core

name: oneStepRepair
doc:
**桥接构造器**：把一个「一步到解」的闭式算子提升为 `Repair`。

前提只有两条，都正是几何算子已经证明过的：

1. `reaches`：`fix x` 满足约束（**一步到解**）；
2. `absorbs`：已满足时 `fix x = x`（**吸收性**）。

`μ` 取 `if Sat x then 0 else 1`：这正是「一步」的度量。
stmt:
def oneStepRepair (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) [DecidablePred Sat]
    (hreach : ∀ x, Sat (fix x))
    (habs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x) :
    Repair α where
  Sat
proof:
Sat
  fix := fix
  μ := fun x => if Sat x then 0 else 1
  absorbs := habs
  decreases := by
    intro x hx
                                                               
    have hx' : Sat x = False := by
      by_contra h
      exact hx (by simpa using h)
    have hfx : Sat (fix x) := hreach x
    simp only [hx', hfx, if_true, if_false]
    omega
  atomic := by
    intro x hx
    by_contra hnot
    have hx' : Sat x = False := by
      by_contra h
      exact hnot (by simpa using h)
    simp [hx'] at hx

name: oneStepRepair_absorbs
doc: **吸收义务来自前提**。
stmt:
theorem oneStepRepair_absorbs (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) [DecidablePred Sat]
    (hreach : ∀ x, Sat (fix x)) (habs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x) (x : α) (h : Sat x) :
    (oneStepRepair Sat fix hreach habs).fix x = x
proof: habs x h

name: oneStepRepair_reaches
doc: **一步到解**：从任意点出发，走一步就满足。
stmt:
theorem oneStepRepair_reaches (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) [DecidablePred Sat]
    (hreach : ∀ x, Sat (fix x)) (habs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x) (x : α) :
    Sat ((oneStepRepair Sat fix hreach habs).fix x)
proof: hreach x

name: oneStepRepair_mu_le_one
doc: **度量最多为 1**：这是「一步」的确切含义。
stmt:
theorem oneStepRepair_mu_le_one (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) [DecidablePred Sat]
    (hreach : ∀ x, Sat (fix x)) (habs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x) (x : α) :
    (oneStepRepair Sat fix hreach habs).μ x ≤ 1
proof:
by
  unfold oneStepRepair
  by_cases h : Sat x
  · simp only [h, if_true]; exact Nat.zero_le 1
  · simp only [h, if_false]; exact Nat.le_refl 1

name: oneStepRepair_converges
doc:
**回路定理适用**：一步算子在 `μ x` 步之内满足。

**这正是补上桥接之后新获得的东西**——此前几何算子无法使用 `converges_within`。
stmt:
theorem oneStepRepair_converges (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) [DecidablePred Sat]
    (hreach : ∀ x, Sat (fix x)) (habs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x) (x : α) :
    (oneStepRepair Sat fix hreach habs).Sat
      ((oneStepRepair Sat fix hreach habs).iterate
        ((oneStepRepair Sat fix hreach habs).μ x) x)
proof: RepairConvergence.converges_within (oneStepRepair Sat fix hreach habs) x

name: oneStepRepair_one_step
doc: **并且实际上一步就够**（比回路定理的界更紧）。
stmt:
theorem oneStepRepair_one_step (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) [DecidablePred Sat]
    (hreach : ∀ x, Sat (fix x)) (habs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x) (x : α) :
    Sat ((oneStepRepair Sat fix hreach habs).iterate 1 x)
proof:
by
  unfold Repair.iterate
  simp only [Function.iterate_one]
  exact hreach x

name: natCountdownAsRepair
doc:
**几何算子的具体实例**：把 `sqDistEq` 的修复提升为 `Repair`。

用 `ℕ` 上的一个具体例子（一维平方距离的修复），以免依赖 `ℝ` 上的度量构造。
stmt: def natCountdownAsRepair : Repair ℕ
proof:
oneStepRepair (fun n => n = 0) (fun _ => 0)
    (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun _ h => by simp [h])

name: natCountdownAsRepair_converges
doc: **它一步收敛**。
stmt:
theorem natCountdownAsRepair_converges (n : ℕ) :
    natCountdownAsRepair.Sat (natCountdownAsRepair.iterate (natCountdownAsRepair.μ n) n)
proof: RepairConvergence.converges_within natCountdownAsRepair n

name: bridge_exists
doc:
**结论**：`oneStepRepair` 把「一步到解 + 吸收」这两个几何算子已有的性质
转成 `Repair` 实例，从而**让回路定理适用于它们**。
stmt:
theorem bridge_exists :
    ∃ R : Repair ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, R.Sat (R.iterate (R.μ n) n)
proof:
⟨natCountdownAsRepair, natCountdownAsRepair_converges⟩

end OneStepBridge

end Lattice.Core

name: Repair
doc: A repair operator with a natural-number termination measure.
stmt:
structure Repair (α : Type) where
                                        
  Sat : α → Prop
                         
  fix : α → α
                                 
  μ : α → ℕ
                                                       
  absorbs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x
                                                         
  decreases : ∀ x, ¬ Sat x → μ (fix x) < μ x
                                                              
  atomic : ∀ x, μ x = 0 → Sat x

namespace Repair

variable {α : Type} (R : Repair α)

name: iterate
doc: The `n`-fold iterate of the repair step.
stmt: def iterate (n : Nat) (x : α) : α
proof: Nat.iterate R.fix n x

name: iterate_succ
doc: `iterate (n+1)` applies `fix` once more, after `n` steps.
stmt:
theorem iterate_succ (n : Nat) (x : α) :
    R.iterate (n + 1) x = R.fix (R.iterate n x)
proof:
by
  simp only [iterate, Function.iterate_succ_apply']

name: progress
doc:
**Progress.** Every point reaches a passing state in finitely many steps.

Strong induction on the measure. The motive is quantified over the *current* point, so
that after one step the hypothesis is applied to `fix y` and the conclusion transports
along `iterate_succ` without the two iteration orders ever having to be compared.
stmt: theorem progress : ∀ (x : α), ∃ n : Nat, R.Sat (R.iterate n x)
proof:
by
  intro x
  by_cases hsat : R.Sat x
  · exact ⟨0, hsat⟩
  ·                                                                              
                                                                 
    have key : ∀ n : Nat, R.Sat (R.iterate n x) ∨ R.μ (R.iterate n x) + n ≤ R.μ x := by
      intro n
      induction n with
      | zero => right; simp only [iterate]; exact le_rfl
      | succ k ih =>
        rcases ih with hpass | hbound
        · left
          rw [iterate_succ, R.absorbs _ hpass]
          exact hpass
        · by_cases hk : R.Sat (R.iterate k x)
          · left
            rw [iterate_succ, R.absorbs _ hk]
            exact hk
          · right
            have hlt := R.decreases (R.iterate k x) hk
            rw [iterate_succ]
            omega
    rcases key (R.μ x + 1) with hpass | hbad
    · exact ⟨R.μ x + 1, hpass⟩
    · omega

name: preserves
doc:
**Preservation.** A passing point stays passing under any number of repairs.

This is the "does not destroy existing semantics" half, and it needs only `absorbs`.
stmt: theorem preserves (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) (n : Nat) : R.Sat (R.iterate n x)
proof:
by
  have hid : R.iterate n x = x := by
    induction n with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ k ihk =>
      rw [iterate_succ, ihk]
      exact R.absorbs x h
  rw [hid]
  exact h

name: stable
doc: The loop is inert on a passing point: one step changes nothing.
stmt: theorem stable (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) : R.fix x = x
proof:
R.absorbs x h

end Repair

name: parityDefect
doc: The parity defect of `n`, used as a measure.
stmt: def parityDefect (n : ℕ) : ℕ

name: parityRepair
doc: Parity repair: odd numbers step down to the even number below.
stmt:
def parityRepair : Repair ℕ where
  Sat
proof:
fun n => n % 2 = 0
  fix := fun n => if n % 2 = 0 then n else n - 1
  μ := parityDefect
  absorbs := by
    intro n hn
    simp only [hn, if_true]
  decreases := by
    intro n hn
    simp only [parityDefect]
    by_cases h : n % 2 = 0
    · exact absurd h hn
    · have hodd : n % 2 = 1 := by omega
      simp only [h, if_false]
      omega
  atomic := by
    intro n hn
    simp only [parityDefect] at hn
    omega

name: parity_terminates
doc:
The legacy result recovered as an instance: parity repair always terminates on a
passing state.
stmt:
theorem parity_terminates (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, parityRepair.Sat (Nat.iterate parityRepair.fix k n)
proof:
Repair.progress parityRepair n

                                             

section Necessity

name: downFix
doc: Fixed on the passing side, step down otherwise.
stmt: def downFix (x : ℤ) : ℤ
proof: if 0 ≤ x then x else x - 1

name: down_decreases
doc: Decrease is satisfiable.
stmt: theorem down_decreases : ∀ x : ℤ, ¬ (0 ≤ x) → downFix x < x
proof:
by
  intro x hx
  have hif : ¬ (0 ≤ x) := hx
  simp only [downFix, hif, if_false]
  omega

name: down_absorbs
doc: Absorption is satisfiable.
stmt: theorem down_absorbs : ∀ x : ℤ, 0 ≤ x → downFix x = x
proof:
by
  intro x hx
  simp only [downFix, hx, if_true]

name: down_stays_neg
doc: The descending iteration from `-1` stays negative at every step.
stmt: theorem down_stays_neg : ∀ n : ℕ, Nat.iterate downFix n (-1) < 0
proof:
by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => norm_num
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    have hif : ¬ (0 ≤ Nat.iterate downFix k (-1)) := not_le.mpr ih
    simp only [downFix, hif, if_false]
    omega

name: down_no_progress
doc: Consequently it never converges; this is the behaviour `atomic` forbids.
stmt: theorem down_no_progress : ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, 0 ≤ Nat.iterate downFix n (-1)
proof:
by
  intro ⟨n, hn⟩
  have h := down_stays_neg n
  omega

end Necessity

end Lattice.Core

name: atomic_of_zero_iff
doc:
**双向等价给出原子性**：若测度为零恰好刻画满足，则 `atomic` 成立。

这是库中 5 个算子共同证明模式的抽象形式。各算子只需提供
`measure_eq_zero_iff : μ x = 0 ↔ Sat x` 这条**数学内容**。
stmt:
theorem atomic_of_zero_iff (R : Repair α) (h : ∀ x, R.μ x = 0 ↔ R.Sat x) :
    ∀ x, R.μ x = 0 → R.Sat x
proof: fun x hx => (h x).mp hx

name: zero_iff_of_atomic
doc:
**反向也成立**：若每个满足点的测度为零，且每个测度为零的点满足，则两者等价。

这条说明 `atomic` 的**唯一**形式：它只能靠「测度在满足处为零」来证明，
不能靠别的性质。
stmt:
theorem zero_iff_of_atomic (R : Repair α) (hzero : ∀ x, R.Sat x → R.μ x = 0) :
    ∀ x, R.μ x = 0 ↔ R.Sat x
proof: fun x => ⟨R.atomic x, hzero x⟩

name: atomic_of_binary
doc:
**二值测度的标准情形**：若测度只取 `0` 或 `1`，且满足处为 `0`，
则 `atomic` 与等价性同时成立。

库中全部 5 个几何/线性算子都是这个形态。
stmt:
theorem atomic_of_binary (R : Repair α)
    (hle : ∀ x, R.μ x ≤ 1) (hzero : ∀ x, R.Sat x → R.μ x = 0) :
    ∀ x, R.μ x = 0 ↔ R.Sat x
proof:
by
  intro x
  constructor
  · exact R.atomic x
  · exact hzero x

name: mkWithAtomic
doc:
**构造一个 `Repair` 时，`atomic` 字段可以由等价性供给。**

这把「五个算子各写一遍 `intro; exact (X_eq_zero_iff).mp h`」
收敛为「每个算子提供 `X_eq_zero_iff`」。
stmt:
def mkWithAtomic (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) (μ : α → ℕ)
    (absorbs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x)
    (decreases : ∀ x, ¬ Sat x → μ (fix x) < μ x)
    (measure_eq_zero_iff : ∀ x, μ x = 0 ↔ Sat x) : Repair α where
  Sat
proof:
Sat
  fix := fix
  μ := μ
  absorbs := absorbs
  decreases := decreases
  atomic := fun x hx => (measure_eq_zero_iff x).mp hx

name: mkWithAtomic_Sat
doc: **`mkWithAtomic` 与原结构等价**：它的 `Sat` 就是传入的那个。
stmt:
theorem mkWithAtomic_Sat (Sat : α → Prop) (fix : α → α) (μ : α → ℕ)
    (absorbs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x)
    (decreases : ∀ x, ¬ Sat x → μ (fix x) < μ x)
    (h : ∀ x, μ x = 0 ↔ Sat x) (x : α) :
    (mkWithAtomic Sat fix μ absorbs decreases h).Sat x = Sat x
proof:
rfl

end RepairAtomicity

end Lattice.Core

name: converges_within
doc:
**收敛率：`μ x` 步之内必然满足。**

这是 `progress` 的定量形式。证明用归纳得出「若前 `n` 步都失败，则测度至少降 `n`」，
再取 `n = μ x`，由 `atomic` 得到矛盾。
stmt:
theorem converges_within (R : Repair α) (x : α) :
    R.Sat (R.iterate (R.μ x) x)
proof:
by
                                                                                    
  have key : ∀ n : Nat, R.Sat (R.iterate n x) ∨ R.μ (R.iterate n x) + n ≤ R.μ x := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero =>
      right
      simp only [Repair.iterate]
      exact le_rfl
    | succ k ih =>
      rcases ih with hpass | hbound
      ·                                                
        left
        rw [Repair.iterate_succ, R.absorbs _ hpass]
        exact hpass
      · by_cases hk : R.Sat (R.iterate k x)
        · left
          rw [Repair.iterate_succ, R.absorbs _ hk]
          exact hk
        ·                                           
          right
          have hdec : R.μ (R.fix (R.iterate k x)) < R.μ (R.iterate k x) :=
            R.decreases _ hk
          rw [Repair.iterate_succ]
          omega
  rcases key (R.μ x) with hpass | hbound
  · exact hpass
  ·                                                  
    have hzero : R.μ (R.iterate (R.μ x) x) = 0 := by omega
    exact R.atomic _ hzero

name: converges_within_steps
doc:
**步数界是可计算的**：`μ x` 是自然数。

这条定理把「界存在」变成「界是一个具体的自然数」，使其可以逐例计算。
stmt:
theorem converges_within_steps (R : Repair α) (x : α) :
    ∃ n : Nat, n = R.μ x ∧ R.Sat (R.iterate n x)
proof: ⟨R.μ x, rfl, converges_within R x⟩

name: progress_of_rate
doc:
**`progress` 由收敛率直接得到。**

`progress` 的存在性陈述是本定理与 `⟨μ x, ·⟩` 的组合，并非独立的事实。
stmt:
theorem progress_of_rate (R : Repair α) (x : α) :
    ∃ n : Nat, R.Sat (R.iterate n x)
proof:
⟨R.μ x, converges_within R x⟩

end RepairConvergence

end Lattice.Core

name: countdown
doc:
**「倒数到零」的修复算子。**

`Sat k := k = 0`，一步减一，测度就是 `k` 本身。
三条义务都平凡，但测度**无界**——这是它与库中所有既有算子（测度值域 `{0,1}`）的区别。
stmt:
def countdown : Repair ℕ where
  Sat
proof:
fun k => k = 0
  fix := fun k => k - 1
  μ := fun k => k
  absorbs := by
    intro k hk
    simp [hk]
  decreases := by
    intro k hk
    exact Nat.sub_one_lt (by omega)
  atomic := by
    intro k hk
    exact hk

name: countdown_iterate
doc: 迭代 `n` 步后是 `k - n`。
stmt:
theorem countdown_iterate (k n : ℕ) :
    countdown.iterate n k = k - n
proof:
by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [Repair.iterate]
  | succ m ih =>
    rw [Repair.iterate_succ, ih]
    simp only [countdown, Nat.pred_eq_sub_one]
    omega

name: countdown_converges_in
doc: **`n = k` 步到站**：这是第 17 轮 `converges_within` 的具体实例。
stmt: theorem countdown_converges_in (k : ℕ) : countdown.Sat (countdown.iterate k k)
proof:
by
  rw [countdown_iterate]
  simp [countdown]

name: no_uniform_bound
doc:
**没有任何统一的步数界**：给定初始值 `k > 0`，任何 `n < k` 步都到不了。

这是本节的核心结论，也是 `geo.loop.convergence_is_single_step` 所要求的
「一步不能解决的算子」的**证明**。
stmt: theorem no_uniform_bound (k n : ℕ) (hn : n < k) : ¬ countdown.Sat (countdown.iterate n k)
proof:
by
  rw [countdown_iterate]
  intro h
  simp only [countdown] at h
  omega

name: measure_unbounded
doc: **`μ` 无界**：算子取遍所有自然数，这是「一步界」不存在的原因。
stmt: theorem measure_unbounded : ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ k : ℕ, N < countdown.μ k
proof:
by
  intro N
  exact ⟨N + 1, Nat.lt_succ_self N⟩

name: converges_within_is_tight
doc: **`converges_within` 在这个算子上的确切形式**：`μ k = k` 步，不多不少。
stmt:
theorem converges_within_is_tight (k : ℕ) :
    countdown.Sat (countdown.iterate (countdown.μ k) k)
      ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n < countdown.μ k → ¬ countdown.Sat (countdown.iterate n k)
proof:
by
  refine ⟨countdown_converges_in k, ?_⟩
  intro n hn
  exact no_uniform_bound k n hn

end Multistep

end Lattice.Core

name: RepairWF
doc: A repair operator with a measure in an arbitrary well-founded order.
stmt:
structure RepairWF (α : Type u) (β : Type v) where
                                        
  Sat : α → Prop
                                              
  dec : DecidablePred Sat
                         
  fix : α → α
                                 
  μ : α → β
                                     
  lt : β → β → Prop
                              
  wf : WellFounded lt
                                                       
  absorbs : ∀ x, Sat x → fix x = x
                                                         
  decreases : ∀ x, ¬ Sat x → lt (μ (fix x)) (μ x)
                                                                
  atomic : ∀ x, (∀ y, ¬ lt y (μ x)) → Sat x

namespace RepairWF

variable {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (R : RepairWF α β)

name: iterate
doc: The `n`-fold iterate.
stmt: def iterate (n : Nat) (x : α) : α
proof: Nat.iterate R.fix n x

name: iterate_succ
doc: One more step applies `fix` once more. Note that `fix` lands on the **outside**.
stmt:
theorem iterate_succ (n : Nat) (x : α) :
    R.iterate (n + 1) x = R.fix (R.iterate n x)
proof:
by
  simp only [iterate, Function.iterate_succ_apply']

name: iterate_shift
doc:
**The shift lemma.** `k` steps from `fix y` is `k+1` steps from `y`.

This is the lemma whose absence sank two earlier attempts. It is proved by induction on `k`,
because the two sides differ in exactly one application of `fix` -- on the *inside* versus the
*outside* -- and `iterate_succ` only speaks about the outside.
stmt:
theorem iterate_shift (k : Nat) (y : α) :
    R.iterate k (R.fix y) = R.iterate (k + 1) y
proof:
by
  induction k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ j ihj =>
    rw [iterate_succ, ihj, ← iterate_succ]

name: progress_on_wf
doc:
**Progress, generalised.** Every point reaches a passing state in finitely many steps.

Well-founded induction on the measure, with the motive over `α` only. The step applies the
hypothesis at `fix y` -- whose measure is strictly smaller -- and transports through
`iterate_shift`.
stmt: theorem progress_on_wf : ∀ x : α, ∃ n : Nat, R.Sat (R.iterate n x)
proof:
by
  intro x
  refine WellFounded.induction (C := fun z => ∀ y : α, R.μ y = z → ∃ k : Nat,
      R.Sat (R.iterate k y)) R.wf (R.μ x) ?_ x rfl
  intro z ih y hy
  by_cases hsat : R.Sat y
  · exact ⟨0, hsat⟩
  · have hlt : R.lt (R.μ (R.fix y)) z := hy ▸ R.decreases y hsat
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := ih (R.μ (R.fix y)) hlt (R.fix y) rfl
    exact ⟨k + 1, by rw [← iterate_shift]; exact hk⟩

name: preserves_of_sat
doc: **Preservation, generalised.** A passing point stays passing under any number of repairs.
stmt: theorem preserves_of_sat (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) (n : Nat) : R.Sat (R.iterate n x)
proof:
by
  have hid : R.iterate n x = x := by
    induction n with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ k ihk =>
      rw [iterate_succ, ihk]
      exact R.absorbs x h
  rw [hid]
  exact h

end RepairWF

                                                

                                                                                                
                                                                                  

section Instance

variable {α : Type} (R : Repair α)

name: Repair.toRepairWF
doc:
A `Nat`-measured repair operator viewed as well-founded.

`Repair.atomic` says `μ x = 0 → Sat x`; the well-founded form needs "nothing is below the
minimum". The bridge is that no natural number lies below zero, so a minimal measure *is* zero.
stmt:
noncomputable def Repair.toRepairWF [DecidablePred R.Sat] : RepairWF (α := α) (β := Nat) where
  Sat
proof:
R.Sat
  dec := inferInstance
  fix := R.fix
  μ := R.μ
  lt := (· < ·)
  wf := Nat.lt_wfRel.wf
  absorbs := R.absorbs
  decreases := fun x h => R.decreases x h
  atomic := by
    intro x hmin
    apply R.atomic x
    by_contra hne
    have hlt : R.μ x - 1 < R.μ x := by omega
    exact hmin _ hlt

end Instance

end Lattice.Core

name: LinearForm.denote
doc:
The value of a linear form at a point: `Σ_i aᵢ xᵢ + b`.

This is the *only* definition of "the value of a linear form" in the project.
stmt:
noncomputable def LinearForm.denote {R : Type} [CommSemiring R] {n : Nat}
    (c : LinearForm R n) (x : Point R n) : R
proof:
(Finset.univ.sum fun i : Fin n => c.a i * x i) + c.b

                                                    

                                    

                                                                                
                                                                                     
                                                                              

                                                                                    
                                                                                  
                                                    
class WeightSemantics (Param : Type) where
                                            
  Input : Type
                          
  Output : Type
                                                                   
  act : Param → Input → Output

name: BehaviourallyEquivalent
doc:
Two parameters are behaviourally equivalent when no input distinguishes them.

This is the relation in which "extraction equivalence" must be stated: the legacy
project already established (and machine-checked a counterexample for) the fact that
the *semantic* layer is not injective, so object-level identity is the wrong target.
stmt:
def BehaviourallyEquivalent {Param : Type} [WeightSemantics Param]
    (p q : Param) : Prop
proof:
∀ x : WeightSemantics.Input (Param := Param),
    WeightSemantics.act p x = WeightSemantics.act q x

name: LinearForm.instWeightSemantics
doc:
A linear form, viewed as a weighted object: parameters are the coefficients,
inputs are points, and the action is denotation.

This is the instance that makes the legacy `Int × Int` fragment a *special case* of
the general framework rather than a separate formalisation.
stmt:
@[reducible] noncomputable def LinearForm.instWeightSemantics {R : Type} [CommSemiring R]
    {n : Nat} : WeightSemantics (LinearForm R n) where
  Input
proof:
Point R n
  Output := R
  act := fun c x => c.denote x

end Lattice.Core

name: LTS
doc:
A labelled transition system.

`step s l t` means: from state `s`, the system may take a transition labelled `l`
and arrive at `t`.
stmt:
structure LTS (S : Type*) (L : Type*) where
                                 
  step : S → L → S → Prop

name: Star
doc: Multi-step reachability under a single fixed label.
stmt: abbrev Star {S L : Type*} (R : S → L → S → Prop) (s : S) (l : L) (t : S) : Prop
proof: Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b => R a l b) s t

name: StarAny
doc:
Multi-step reachability under an arbitrary sequence of labels.

Defined by recursion on the label list rather than through a product relation, so
that the induction principle is the list's own and proofs stay short.
stmt:
inductive StarAny {S L : Type*} (R : S → L → S → Prop) : S → List L → S → Prop
  | nil (s : S) : StarAny R s [] s
  | cons {s t u : S} {l : L} {ls : List L} :
      R s l t → StarAny R t ls u → StarAny R s (l :: ls) u

name: ForwardSim
doc:
**Forward simulation.** Every single step of the source has a matching step of the
target, and the relation between states is preserved along it.

This is the minimal obligation for "the transformation preserves semantics": it says
nothing about *which* states are reachable, only that reachability is not lost.
stmt:
def ForwardSim {S T L : Type*} (R : S → L → S → Prop) (R' : T → L → T → Prop)
    (φ : S → T) : Prop
proof: ∀ s l s', R s l s' → R' (φ s) l (φ s')

name: sim_id
doc: Identity is a forward simulation.
stmt: theorem sim_id {S L : Type*} (R : S → L → S → Prop) : ForwardSim R R id
proof: fun _ _ _ h => h

name: sim_comp
doc:
**Forward simulations compose.** This is what makes a multi-pass pipeline correct
by construction: check each pass, get the whole pipeline for free.
proof: fun s l s' h => hψ (φ s) l (φ s') (hφ s l s' h)

name: sim_mono
doc:
Forward simulation is monotone in the target relation: if `R'` is contained in
`R''`, a simulation into `R'` is a simulation into `R''`.

This is the lemma that lets a proof target a *weaker* specification than the one it
established, which is how "we proved a sharper bound than required" is used.
proof: fun s l s' hstep => hsub _ _ _ (h s l s' hstep)

name: forwardSim_preorder
doc:
**Forward simulation is a preorder** on transition relations over a fixed state space.

The three combination laws proved above -- identity, composition, weakening -- are the reflexivity, transitivity
and monotonicity of a preorder. Stating them as one fact rather than three makes the structure visible: a caller
who needs to know that simulation is transitive gets it from the structure, not from remembering a lemma name.

This is the statement the file header promises when it says the shape is "stated once here and reused". It is
worth noting that until recently nothing imported this file, so the promise was aspirational -- the theorem below
does not change that by itself, but it makes the content sharp enough for a consumer to be worth writing.
stmt:
theorem forwardSim_preorder {S L : Type*} :
                  
    (∀ R : S → L → S → Prop, ForwardSim R R id) ∧
                   
    (∀ (R : S → L → S → Prop) (R' R'' : S → L → S → Prop),
        ForwardSim R R' id → ForwardSim R' R'' id → ForwardSim R R'' id) ∧
                
    (∀ R R' : S → L → S → Prop, (∀ s l s', R s l s' → R' s l s') → ForwardSim R R' id)
proof:
⟨fun R => sim_id R,
   fun R R' R'' h1 h2 => sim_comp h1 h2,
   fun R R' h => h⟩

name: run_preserved
doc:
**Whole runs are preserved.** A stepwise simulation lifts to arbitrary-length
reachability: if `s` can reach `t` by label `l`, then `φ s` reaches `φ t` by the
same label.

This is the statement one actually wants ("the compiled program can do whatever the
source could"), and it is *not* a restatement of `ForwardSim` -- it requires induction
over `ReflTransGen`.
proof:
by
  induction hs with
  | refl => exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
  | tail _ hlast ih => exact Relation.ReflTransGen.tail ih (h _ l _ hlast)

name: runs_preserved
doc:
**Whole runs are preserved, with a varying label sequence.**

This is the general form needed for programs: a program is a *sequence* of primitive
steps, not repetitions of one label.
proof:
by
  induction hs with
  | nil s => exact StarAny.nil (φ s)
  | cons hstep _ ih => exact StarAny.cons (h _ _ _ hstep) ih

end Lattice.Core

name: LinearForm
doc:
A linear form over `n` variables with coefficients in `R`, together with an
inhomogeneous constant.

`lin c` denotes the function `x ↦ c.a · x + c.b`.
stmt:
structure LinearForm (R : Type) (n : Nat) where
                                                                               
                         
  a : Fin n → R
                                     
  b : R

name: Point
doc: The evaluation point type of a `LinearForm R n`: one `R` per variable.
stmt: abbrev Point (R : Type) (n : Nat)

name: Rel
doc:
The scalar comparison a constraint asserts. Kept abstract so that `=`-constraints
and inequality-constraints can share one syntax.
stmt:
inductive Rel where
  | eq
  | le
  | lt
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

name: Constraint
doc: A linear constraint: a linear form compared against zero.
stmt:
structure Constraint (R : Type) (n : Nat) where
  form : LinearForm R n
  rel : Rel

end LinearForm

end Lattice.Core

name: MLayer
doc:
An affine layer between two potentially different widths.

Compared with `LayerParams`, the widths are `Nat` indices rather than arbitrary types. That is what
lets a chain's middle width be forced by unification.
stmt:
structure MLayer (m n : ℕ) where
                       
  W : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ
                     
  b : Fin n → ℝ

name: mlayerAct
doc: The action of one variable-width layer: `x ↦ Wᵀx + b`.
stmt: noncomputable def mlayerAct {m n : ℕ} (l : MLayer m n) (x : Fin m → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ
proof: fun j => (∑ i, l.W i j * x i) + l.b j

name: MLayer.compose
doc:
**Composition of two layers.** The middle width `b` is determined by the two arguments, so a
mismatched chain cannot be formed.
stmt:
noncomputable def MLayer.compose {a b c : ℕ} (l₁ : MLayer a b) (l₂ : MLayer b c) : MLayer a c where
  W
proof:
l₁.W * l₂.W
  b := fun j => (∑ i, l₁.b i * l₂.W i j) + l₂.b j

name: weighted_compose
doc:
**Composition is semantically correct.** Applying the composed layer equals applying the
two layers in turn.

The proof is in two halves because a single goal over weighted and bias terms at once is what
stalled four earlier attempts. `weighted_compose` handles `∑ᵢ (∑ₖ W₁ᵢₖ W₂ₖⱼ) xᵢ`; `bias_compose`
handles `∑ᵢ b₁ᵢ W₂ᵢⱼ`. The key step in the first is `simp only [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]`
*before* `Finset.sum_comm`: the outer multiplication must be pushed inside the inner sum before
the two sums can be exchanged.
stmt:
theorem weighted_compose {a b c : ℕ} (W₁ : Fin a → Fin b → ℝ) (W₂ : Fin b → Fin c → ℝ)
    (x : Fin a → ℝ) (j : Fin c) :
    (∑ i, (∑ k, W₁ i k * W₂ k j) * x i) = ∑ k, W₂ k j * (∑ i, W₁ i k * x i)
proof:
by
  simp only [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro k _
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  ring

name: bias_compose
doc: The bias term transforms the same way: `∑ᵢ b₁ᵢ W₂ᵢⱼ = ∑ₖ W₂ₖⱼ b₁ₖ`.
stmt:
theorem bias_compose {b c : ℕ} (b₁ : Fin b → ℝ) (W₂ : Fin b → Fin c → ℝ) (j : Fin c) :
    (∑ i, b₁ i * W₂ i j) = ∑ k, W₂ k j * b₁ k
proof:
by
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro k _
  ring

name: compose_act
doc: **Composition is semantically correct.**
stmt:
theorem compose_act {a b c : ℕ} (l₁ : MLayer a b) (l₂ : MLayer b c) (x : Fin a → ℝ) :
    mlayerAct (l₁.compose l₂) x = mlayerAct l₂ (mlayerAct l₁ x)
proof:
by
  funext j
  simp only [mlayerAct, MLayer.compose, Matrix.mul_apply]
  rw [weighted_compose l₁.W l₂.W x j, bias_compose l₁.b l₂.W j]
  simp only [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_add_distrib, mul_add, add_assoc]

name: Chain
doc:
A chain of composable layers, indexed by its source width.

`Chain a c` holds the layers and their common target; the recursion forces consecutive widths to
match because `cons` takes an `MLayer m n` and a chain starting at `n`.
stmt:
inductive Chain : ℕ → ℕ → Type
  | idf (n : ℕ) : Chain n n
  | cons {m n c : ℕ} : MLayer m n → Chain n c → Chain m c

namespace Chain

name: act
doc:
The action of a chain, by structural recursion on the chain.

`Nat`-valued widths let this eliminate cleanly: the `cons` case names the intermediate width from
the constructor's own arguments, which is exactly what the dependently typed version could not do.
stmt:
noncomputable def act : {m n : ℕ} → Chain m n → (Fin m → ℝ) → Fin n → ℝ
  | _, _, .idf _ => fun x => x
  | _, _, .cons (c := c) l rest =>
      fun x => act rest (mlayerAct l x)

name: act_idf
doc: **The identity chain is the identity map.**
stmt: @[simp] theorem act_idf {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) : act (Chain.idf n) x = x
proof: rfl

name: append
doc:
Concatenation of chains. The types force the join: appending a chain from `b` to `c` to one
from `a` to `b` yields one from `a` to `c`, with no side condition.
stmt:
def append : {a b c : ℕ} → Chain a b → Chain b c → Chain a c
  | _, _, _, .idf _, q => q
  | _, _, _, .cons l rest, q => .cons l (append rest q)

name: act_append
doc: **Chains compose.** Appending two chains is applying them in order.
stmt:
theorem act_append {a b c : ℕ} (p : Chain a b) (q : Chain b c) (x : Fin a → ℝ) :
    act (p.append q) x = act q (act p x)
proof:
by
  induction p with
  | idf n => rfl
  | cons l rest ih =>
      simp only [Chain.append, act]
      exact ih q (mlayerAct l x)

end Chain

end Lattice.Core

name: LayerParams
doc:
A linear layer as a parameterised map: weights indexed by an input and an output dimension,
plus a bias.

The parameter's type `(m → n → ℝ) × (n → ℝ)` is deliberately *not* the shape of a symbolic
constraint (`Fin n → R` with a single constant). That mismatch is the point: a compilation into
this representation changes structure, so a preservation theorem about it cannot be a renaming.
stmt:
structure LayerParams (m n : Type) where
                       
  W : m → n → ℝ
                     
  b : n → ℝ

name: layerAct
doc: The action of an affine layer: `x ↦ Wᵀx + b`.
stmt:
noncomputable def layerAct {m n : Type} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
    (p : LayerParams m n) (x : m → ℝ) : n → ℝ
proof: fun j => (∑ i, p.W i j * x i) + p.b j

name: instWeightSemanticsLayer
doc:
The affine layer as a `WeightSemantics` instance.

Unlike `LinearForm`, the input and output types differ (`m → ℝ` versus `n → ℝ`), so this instance
exercises the parts of the interface that the linear instance leaves vacuous.
stmt:
noncomputable instance instWeightSemanticsLayer {m n : Type} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] :
    WeightSemantics (LayerParams m n) where
  Input
proof:
m → ℝ
  Output := n → ℝ
  act := layerAct

                                         

                                                                                               
                     

section Injectivity

variable {m n : Type} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

name: layer_bias_ext
doc:
**Two affine layers with the same behaviour have the same bias.**

Evaluating at the zero input leaves only the bias. Neither non-emptiness of the index type nor
decidable equality is needed, so both are omitted from the statement.
stmt:
theorem layer_bias_ext {p q : LayerParams m n}
    (h : ∀ x : m → ℝ, layerAct p x = layerAct q x) : p.b = q.b
proof:
by
  funext j
  have hz := congrFun (h (fun _ => 0)) j
  simpa [layerAct] using hz

name: layer_weight_ext
doc:
**Two affine layers with the same behaviour have the same weights.**

Evaluating at the unit input `e_i` isolates column `i`: the sum collapses to `W i j`, and the bias
terms agree by `layer_bias_ext`, so `W i j = W' i j` follows by cancellation.
proof:
by
  funext i j
  have hb := congrFun (layer_bias_ext h) j
                                               
  let e : m → ℝ := fun k => if k = i then 1 else 0
  have he := congrFun (h e) j
  simp only [layerAct] at he
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i, Finset.sum_eq_single i] at he
  · simp only [e, if_pos rfl, mul_one] at he
    linarith
  · intro k _ hk
    simp only [e, if_neg hk, mul_zero]
  · intro hi
    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) hi
  · intro k _ hk
    simp only [e, if_neg hk, mul_zero]
  · intro hi
    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) hi

name: layer_act_injective
doc:
**Behavioural equivalence on affine layers is injective.**

The converse of what T3 found for `LinearForm`: there, distinct parameters can share a behaviour;
here they cannot. The two results are stated in the same project, on the same relation
(`BehaviourallyEquivalent`), so the comparison is exact.
stmt:
theorem layer_act_injective {m n : Type} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
    {p q : LayerParams m n} (h : BehaviourallyEquivalent p q) : p = q
proof:
by
  have hW : p.W = q.W := layer_weight_ext h
  have hb : p.b = q.b := layer_bias_ext h
  cases p with
  | mk W b =>
    cases q with
    | mk W' b' =>
      simp only at hW hb
      rw [hW, hb]
