name: Pt
doc:
A point of `n`-dimensional real space.

This is `Lattice.Core.Syntax.Point` at `R = ℝ`, not a new abbreviation: defining a second `Point` would be
the exact duplication `Core` exists to prevent, and invariant I3 caught an earlier revision doing it.
stmt: abbrev Pt (n : ℕ)
proof: Lattice.Core.Point ℝ n

name: GeoExpr
doc:
**Geometric polynomial expressions.**

Atoms are the coordinates of numbered points; the operations are addition, subtraction and
multiplication. There is no `div` and no `sqrt` -- see the module docstring.

The expression depends on `n` (the ambient dimension) but *not* on how many points the configuration
has, so the same constraint can be interpreted in any configuration.
stmt:
inductive GeoExpr (n : ℕ) : Type where
                                                      
  | coord (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n)
                         
  | const (c : ℝ)
  | add (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)
  | sub (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)
  | mul (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)

namespace GeoExpr

variable {n : ℕ}

name: zero
doc: Zero as an expression. Convenient as a right-hand side for "this vanishes".
stmt: def zero : GeoExpr n
proof: .const 0

name: one
doc: One as an expression.
stmt: def one : GeoExpr n
proof: .const 1

name: evalPts
doc:
**Evaluation** in a configuration, i.e. for a family of points.

The interpretation is a function `ℕ → Pt n`: point index to coordinates. Coordinates are addressed
directly (`pts p axis`), which is what `IRExpr` could not do for the second component.
stmt: noncomputable def evalPts (e : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℝ
proof:
match e with
  | .coord p axis => pts p axis
  | .const c => c
  | .add e₁ e₂ => e₁.evalPts pts + e₂.evalPts pts
  | .sub e₁ e₂ => e₁.evalPts pts - e₂.evalPts pts
  | .mul e₁ e₂ => e₁.evalPts pts * e₂.evalPts pts

name: evalPts_coord
stmt:
@[simp] theorem evalPts_coord (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (coord p axis).evalPts pts = pts p axis
proof: rfl

name: evalPts_const
stmt: @[simp] theorem evalPts_const (c : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : (const c).evalPts pts = c
proof: rfl

name: evalPts_add
stmt:
@[simp] theorem evalPts_add (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (e₁.add e₂).evalPts pts = e₁.evalPts pts + e₂.evalPts pts
proof: rfl

name: evalPts_sub
stmt:
@[simp] theorem evalPts_sub (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (e₁.sub e₂).evalPts pts = e₁.evalPts pts - e₂.evalPts pts
proof: rfl

name: evalPts_mul
stmt:
@[simp] theorem evalPts_mul (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (e₁.mul e₂).evalPts pts = e₁.evalPts pts * e₂.evalPts pts
proof: rfl

name: evalPts_zero
stmt: @[simp] theorem evalPts_zero (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : (zero : GeoExpr n).evalPts pts = 0
proof: rfl

name: evalPts_one
stmt: @[simp] theorem evalPts_one (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : (one : GeoExpr n).evalPts pts = 1
proof: rfl

name: evalPts_sub_eq_zero_iff
doc:
The difference of two expressions vanishing is the same as the two values being equal.

This is the form every equality constraint reduces to, and it is `rfl`-adjacent, which is why it is
recorded: `eval a = eval b ↔ eval (sub a b) = 0` is what lets a constraint be turned into a
polynomial whose zero set is the solution set.
stmt:
theorem evalPts_sub_eq_zero_iff (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (e₁.sub e₂).evalPts pts = 0 ↔ e₁.evalPts pts = e₂.evalPts pts
proof:
by
  simp [sub_eq_zero]

end GeoExpr

end Lattice.Geo

name: GeoExpr.maxPoint
doc:
**The largest point index an expression mentions.** A carrier with more than this many points can read the
expression; that is exactly the bound the differentiability statement needs.
stmt:
def GeoExpr.maxPoint : GeoExpr n → ℕ
  | .coord p _ => p
  | .const _ => 0
  | .add e₁ e₂ => max (maxPoint e₁) (maxPoint e₂)
  | .sub e₁ e₂ => max (maxPoint e₁) (maxPoint e₂)
  | .mul e₁ e₂ => max (maxPoint e₁) (maxPoint e₂)

name: maxPoint_lt_of_coord
doc:
**A flattened configuration reads every point the expression mentions**, given `maxPoint e < k`.

This is the bridge between the side condition and the carrier: it is what lets each `coord` case of the induction
produce a projection instead of getting stuck.
stmt:
theorem maxPoint_lt_of_coord {e : GeoExpr n} {p : ℕ} {axis : Fin n}
    (h : GeoExpr.coord p axis = e) (hk : GeoExpr.maxPoint e < k) : p < k
proof:
by
  subst h
  simpa [GeoExpr.maxPoint] using hk

name: toNatConfig
doc:
**A finite configuration read as an `ℕ`-indexed one**, filling the remaining points with the origin.

The bridge between the flattened carrier (where analysis works) and `evalPts`'s own domain. Points beyond `k`
are never read, because `maxPoint e < k` bounds every index an expression can mention.
stmt: noncomputable def toNatConfig (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) : ℕ → Pt n
proof: fun p => if h : p < k then unflatten w ⟨p, h⟩ else 0

name: derivExpr
doc:
**The derivative of an expression's evaluation, as a continuous linear functional on the flattened carrier.**

Defined by recursion so that `hasFDerivAt_eval` is an induction rather than a definition unfolding. The `mul`
case carries the product rule verbatim, which is why the operator-valued recursion closes.
stmt:
noncomputable def derivExpr (k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    (Fin (k * n) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ
proof:
match e with
  | .coord p axis =>
    if h : p < k then coordProj k n ⟨p, h⟩ axis else 0
  | .const _ => 0
  | .add e₁ e₂ => derivExpr k e₁ w + derivExpr k e₂ w
  | .sub e₁ e₂ => derivExpr k e₁ w - derivExpr k e₂ w
  | .mul e₁ e₂ =>
    e₂.evalPts (toNatConfig w) • derivExpr k e₁ w
      + e₁.evalPts (toNatConfig w) • derivExpr k e₂ w

name: maxPoint_le_add_left
doc: **Every subexpression's points are within the whole's bound.**
stmt: theorem maxPoint_le_add_left {e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n} : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₁ ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint (.add e₁ e₂)
proof:
by
  simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint]

name: maxPoint_le_sub_left
stmt: theorem maxPoint_le_sub_left {e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n} : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₁ ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint (.sub e₁ e₂)
proof:
by
  simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint]

name: maxPoint_le_mul_left
stmt: theorem maxPoint_le_mul_left {e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n} : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₁ ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint (.mul e₁ e₂)
proof:
by
  simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint]

name: lt_of_le_maxPoint
doc: **A point index below the whole's bound is below `k`.**
stmt:
theorem lt_of_le_maxPoint {e : GeoExpr n} {p : ℕ} (h : p ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint e)
    (hk : GeoExpr.maxPoint e < k) : p < k
proof: lt_of_le_of_lt h hk

name: maxPoint_lt_of_le
doc: **A subexpression's bound follows from the whole's.**
stmt:
theorem maxPoint_lt_of_le {e : GeoExpr n} {p : ℕ} (hp : p ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint e)
    (hk : GeoExpr.maxPoint e < k) : p < k
proof: lt_of_le_of_lt hp hk

name: evalPts_coord_of_lt
doc:
**A configuration reads a coordinate the same way on both carriers.**

The link between `evalPts` (on `ℕ → Pt n`) and `unflatten` (on the flattened carrier): for a point index within
the bound, the two agree.
proof:
by
  show toNatConfig w p axis = unflatten w ⟨p, hpk⟩ axis
  unfold toNatConfig
  rw [dif_pos hpk]

name: hasFDerivAt_eval
doc:
**Every expression is differentiable on a carrier large enough to read it.**

The bound `maxPoint e < k` is the content of "large enough": an expression mentioning point `k` has no place to
live on a carrier with `k` points, and the `coord` case would have to produce a projection for a point that does
not exist.

The induction is structural. `coord` cites `Lattice.Geo.Differentiable.hasFDerivAt_coord`; `const` is constant;
`add` and `sub` combine by linearity; `mul` uses the product rule with the subexpressions' values as
coefficients, which are themselves differentiable by the induction hypotheses.
stmt:
theorem hasFDerivAt_eval (k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (hk : GeoExpr.maxPoint e < k)
    (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => e.evalPts (toNatConfig y)) (derivExpr k e w) w
proof:
by
  induction e with
  | coord p axis =>
                                                                           
    by_cases hpk : p < k
    · have := hasFDerivAt_coord (k := k) (n := n) ⟨p, hpk⟩ axis w
                                                                                                
      simpa [derivExpr, dif_pos hpk, toNatConfig, dif_pos hpk] using this
    · exact absurd (lt_of_le_of_lt (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] : p ≤ GeoExpr.maxPoint (.coord p axis)) hk) hpk
  | const c =>
                                     
    simpa [derivExpr] using
      (hasFDerivAt_const (c : ℝ) (x := w) : HasFDerivAt (fun _ : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => c) 0 w)
  | add e₁ e₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    have h₁ := ih₁ (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega)
    have h₂ := ih₂ (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega)
    simpa [derivExpr, GeoExpr.evalPts] using h₁.add h₂
  | sub e₁ e₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    have h₁ := ih₁ (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega)
    have h₂ := ih₂ (by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega)
    simpa [derivExpr, GeoExpr.evalPts] using h₁.sub h₂
  | mul e₁ e₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    have hk₁ : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₁ < k := by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega
    have hk₂ : GeoExpr.maxPoint e₂ < k := by simp [GeoExpr.maxPoint] at hk ⊢; omega
    have h₁ := ih₁ hk₁
    have h₂ := ih₂ hk₂
                                                                                               
    have hmul := h₁.mul h₂
    simpa [derivExpr, GeoExpr.evalPts, smul_eq_mul, add_comm]

name: evalPts_hasNonzeroDeriv
doc:
**A non-vanishing derivative of `evalPts` is exactly `HasNonzeroDeriv`**, because `hasFDerivAt_eval` already
supplies the `HasFDerivAt` half with `derivExpr k e w` as the derivative.
stmt:
theorem evalPts_hasNonzeroDeriv
    (k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (hk : e.maxPoint < k) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ)
    (hne : derivExpr k e w ≠ 0) :
    HasNonzeroDeriv (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => e.evalPts (toNatConfig y)) w
proof: ⟨derivExpr k e w, hne, hasFDerivAt_eval k e hk w⟩

name: evalPts_localMin_implies_zero
doc:
**The expression penalty's local-minimum guarantee.**

With the derivative non-vanishing, a local minimum of the squared penalty forces the penalty to vanish -- so the
configuration satisfies the expression equation exactly. Without that hypothesis the statement is false: a constant
expression minimizes its own penalty everywhere and equals its constant, which need not be zero.

The two halves come from the two modules: `hasFDerivAt_eval` (differentiation) and `localMin_implies_zero`
(first-order optimality).
stmt:
theorem evalPts_localMin_implies_zero
    (k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (hk : e.maxPoint < k) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ)
    (hne : derivExpr k e w ≠ 0)
    (hmin : IsLocalMin
      (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => (e.evalPts (toNatConfig y)) ^ 2) w) :
    e.evalPts (toNatConfig w) = 0
proof:
localMin_implies_zero (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => e.evalPts (toNatConfig y)) w
    (evalPts_hasNonzeroDeriv k e hk w hne) hmin

name: constExpr_localMin_counterexample
doc:
**A constant expression is the counterexample the hypothesis excludes**, stated so the boundary above is not
merely asserted: every point is a local minimum of its squared penalty, and the penalty equals the constant
everywhere rather than vanishing.
stmt:
theorem constExpr_localMin_counterexample
    (c : ℝ) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    IsLocalMin (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => ((GeoExpr.const c).evalPts (toNatConfig y)) ^ 2) w
proof:
by
  have hconst : ∀ y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ, (GeoExpr.const c).evalPts (toNatConfig y) = c := by
    intro y
    simp [GeoExpr.evalPts]
  simp only [hconst]
  exact isLocalMin_const

end Lattice.Geo

name: cofactor
doc:
**A 2×2 minor of the matrix with rows `u` and `v`.**

In `n = 2` this is (up to sign) the cross product; in general, the collection of all minors is the Plücker
coordinate of the line spanned by the two vectors.
stmt: noncomputable def cofactor (u v : Pt n) (i j : Fin n) : ℝ
proof: u i * v j - u j * v i

name: cofactor_swap
doc:
**The minor is alternating in the index pair**: swapping the indices negates it. This is what makes the
collection a Plücker coordinate rather than an arbitrary list of numbers.
stmt:
theorem cofactor_swap (u v : Pt n) (i j : Fin n) :
    cofactor u v j i = -cofactor u v i j
proof:
by
  unfold cofactor
  ring

name: cofactor_diag
doc: **The minor vanishes on the diagonal**, since a vector is always proportional to itself.
stmt: theorem cofactor_diag (u v : Pt n) (i : Fin n) : cofactor u v i i = 0
proof:
by
  unfold cofactor
  ring

name: pluckerNorm
doc:
**The squared norm of the wedge** `u ∧ v`: the sum of squares of all 2×2 minors.

Zero exactly when the two vectors are dependent; that characterisation is `Lattice.Geo.Plucker.pluckerNorm_eq_zero_iff`.
stmt: noncomputable def pluckerNorm (u v : Pt n) : ℝ
proof: ∑ i, ∑ j, (cofactor u v i j) ^ 2

name: pluckerNorm_nonneg
doc: **The Plücker norm is non-negative**, so it is a legitimate loss.
stmt: theorem pluckerNorm_nonneg (u v : Pt n) : 0 ≤ pluckerNorm u v
proof:
by
  unfold pluckerNorm
  positivity

name: collinearPenalty
doc:
**`collinear`'s penalty**: the Plücker norm of the two segments.

`collinear a b c` asserts `seg b a` lies on the line through `seg c a`, which is exactly dependence of those two
segments.
stmt: noncomputable def collinearPenalty (a b c : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℝ
proof: pluckerNorm (GeoConstraint.seg pts a b) (GeoConstraint.seg pts a c)

name: parallelPenalty
doc: **`parallel`'s penalty**: the Plücker norm of the two segments being compared.
stmt: noncomputable def parallelPenalty (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℝ
proof: pluckerNorm (GeoConstraint.seg pts a b) (GeoConstraint.seg pts c e)

name: collinearPenalty_nonneg
doc: **Both existential penalties are non-negative.**
stmt: theorem collinearPenalty_nonneg (a b c : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : 0 ≤ collinearPenalty a b c pts
proof: pluckerNorm_nonneg _ _

name: parallelPenalty_nonneg
stmt: theorem parallelPenalty_nonneg (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : 0 ≤ parallelPenalty a b c e pts
proof:
pluckerNorm_nonneg _ _

                       

                                                

                                                                                                      
                                                                                                              
                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                 

  

end Lattice.Geo

name: crossOf
doc:
**A 2×2 minor relating the segments `a→b` and `c→e`**, indexed on `ℕ`.

`Lattice.Geo.Exterior.cofactor` takes two vectors `Pt n`; here the vectors are those two segments of a configuration,
and the indices are `ℕ` because that is what `GeoConstraint.seg` uses.
stmt: noncomputable def crossOf (a b c e : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℝ
proof:
GeoConstraint.seg pts a b i * GeoConstraint.seg pts c e j
    - GeoConstraint.seg pts a b j * GeoConstraint.seg pts c e i

name: toNatConfig_apply
doc:
**`toNatConfig` agrees with `unflatten` on the carrier.**

`k` is inferred from the carrier type of `v`, so it is not a named argument; the definition is unfolded with
`show` and the bound is discharged by `p.isLt`.
stmt:
theorem toNatConfig_apply {k : ℕ} (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) (p : Fin k) :
    toNatConfig v p = unflatten v p
proof:
by
  show (if h : p.val < k then unflatten v ⟨p.val, h⟩ else 0) = unflatten v p
  rw [dif_pos p.isLt]

name: toNatConfig_eq_zero_of_ge
doc: **`toNatConfig` is the origin beyond the carrier**, so it is constant -- hence smooth -- there.
stmt:
theorem toNatConfig_eq_zero_of_ge {k : ℕ} (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : k ≤ p) :
    toNatConfig v p = 0
proof:
by
  show (if h : p < k then unflatten v ⟨p, h⟩ else 0) = 0
  rw [dif_neg (Nat.not_lt.mpr hp)]

name: differentiable_segCompFin
doc: **A segment component is differentiable for `Fin k` indices.**
stmt:
theorem differentiable_segCompFin {k : ℕ} (a b : Fin k) (i : Fin n) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ =>
      GeoConstraint.seg (toNatConfig v) a.val b.val i)
proof:
by
  have h : (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => GeoConstraint.seg (toNatConfig v) a.val b.val i)
      = fun v => segComp (n := n) a b i v := by
    funext v
    simp only [GeoConstraint.seg, segComp, toNatConfig_apply]
  rw [h]
  exact differentiable_segComp (n := n) a b i

name: differentiable_toNatConfig_coord
doc:
**A coordinate of `toNatConfig` is differentiable for arbitrary `ℕ` indices.**

Inside the carrier this is `coordProj`; beyond it the value is the constant `0`. Both are smooth, and splitting on
the bound is what makes the two cases available.
stmt:
theorem differentiable_toNatConfig_coord {k : ℕ} (p : ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => toNatConfig v p i)
proof:
by
  by_cases hp : p < k
  ·                                                                             
    have h : (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => toNatConfig v p i)
        = fun v => unflatten v ⟨p, hp⟩ i := by
      funext v
      simp only [toNatConfig, dif_pos hp]
    rw [h]
    exact differentiable_coord (n := n) ⟨p, hp⟩ i
  ·                              
    have hzero : ∀ v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ, toNatConfig v p = 0 :=
      fun v => toNatConfig_eq_zero_of_ge v p (Nat.not_lt.mp hp)
    have h : (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => toNatConfig v p i) = fun _ => (0 : ℝ) := by
      funext v
      rw [hzero v]
      rfl
    rw [h]
    exact differentiable_const 0

name: differentiable_segCompNat
doc:
**A segment component is differentiable for *arbitrary* `ℕ` indices**, being a difference of two
coordinates.
stmt:
theorem differentiable_segCompNat {k : ℕ} (a b : ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => GeoConstraint.seg (toNatConfig v) a b i)
proof:
by
  have h : (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => GeoConstraint.seg (toNatConfig v) a b i)
      = fun v => toNatConfig v b i - toNatConfig v a i := by
    funext v
    simp only [GeoConstraint.seg]
  rw [h]
  exact (differentiable_toNatConfig_coord b i).sub (differentiable_toNatConfig_coord a i)

name: differentiable_crossOfFn
doc: **A Plücker minor is differentiable**: a difference of two products of segment components.
stmt:
theorem differentiable_crossOfFn {k : ℕ} (a b c e : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => crossOf (n := n) a b c e i j (toNatConfig v))
proof:
((differentiable_segCompNat a b i).mul (differentiable_segCompNat c e j)).sub
    ((differentiable_segCompNat a b j).mul (differentiable_segCompNat c e i))

name: differentiable_pluckerOfFn
doc: **The Plücker norm of two segments is differentiable**: a sum of squared minors.
stmt:
theorem differentiable_pluckerOfFn {k : ℕ} (a b c e : ℕ) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ =>
      ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin n, (crossOf (n := n) a b c e i j (toNatConfig v)) ^ 2)
proof:
Differentiable.sum (fun i _ =>
    Differentiable.sum (fun j _ => (differentiable_crossOfFn a b c e i j).pow 2))

name: differentiable_collinearPenalty
doc:
**The collinearity penalty is differentiable.**

`collinearPenalty a b c pts` is `pluckerNorm (seg a b) (seg a c)`, and `pluckerNorm` is the double sum of squared
minors -- so the statement is the previous one with the segments identified, which is `simp` plus the two
`unfold`s that relate `Exterior`'s spelling to this file's.
stmt:
theorem differentiable_collinearPenalty {k : ℕ} (a b c : ℕ) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ =>
      collinearPenalty (n := n) a b c (toNatConfig v))
proof:
by
  have h : (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => collinearPenalty (n := n) a b c (toNatConfig v))
      = fun v => ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin n,
          (crossOf (n := n) a b a c i j (toNatConfig v)) ^ 2 := by
    funext v
    simp only [collinearPenalty, pluckerNorm, cofactor, crossOf]
  rw [h]
  exact differentiable_pluckerOfFn a b a c

name: differentiable_parallelPenalty
doc: **The parallel penalty is differentiable**, by the same identification.
stmt:
theorem differentiable_parallelPenalty {k : ℕ} (a b c e : ℕ) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ =>
      parallelPenalty (n := n) a b c e (toNatConfig v))
proof:
by
  have h : (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => parallelPenalty (n := n) a b c e (toNatConfig v))
      = fun v => ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin n,
          (crossOf (n := n) a b c e i j (toNatConfig v)) ^ 2 := by
    funext v
    simp only [parallelPenalty, pluckerNorm, cofactor, crossOf]
  rw [h]
  exact differentiable_pluckerOfFn a b c e

end Lattice.Geo

name: configOf
doc:
**The configuration a weight vector denotes.**

The object-layer extraction: since `flatten` is a bijection there is nothing to search for.
stmt: noncomputable def configOf (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) : Fin k → Pt n
proof: unflatten v

name: configOf_roundtrip
doc: Round-tripping a vector through a configuration returns it. The object layer is exact.
stmt:
@[simp] theorem configOf_roundtrip (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    flatten (configOf v) = v
proof: flatten_unflatten v

name: configOf_inv
doc: Round-tripping a configuration through a vector returns it.
stmt:
@[simp] theorem configOf_inv (pts : Fin k → Pt n) :
    configOf (flatten pts) = pts
proof: unflatten_flatten pts

name: satisfies
doc:
**Which constraints a weight vector satisfies.**

The verification predicate: a constraint holds at `v` when its evaluation is true at the configuration `v`
denotes.

Stated for `GeoConstraint`, the type that includes both the polynomial and the square layer, so that the
verification loop can ask about `collinear` and `perpendicular` as well as `sqDistEq`.
stmt: noncomputable def satisfies (c : GeoConstraint n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : Prop
proof: GeoConstraint.Holds c pts

name: perp_neg_invariant
doc:
**Negation preserves perpendicularity.** `dot (-u) (-v) = dot u v`, so a reflection through the
origin cannot be detected by a perpendicularity constraint -- only distances notice it as well, and
distances are preserved too.
stmt:
theorem perp_neg_invariant (a b c e : Fin k) (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, seg a b i (-v) * seg c e i (-v)) = ∑ i, seg a b i v * seg c e i v
proof:
by
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  unfold seg
  simp only [unflatten, Pi.neg_apply]
  ring

name: perp_neg_iff
doc:
**The perpendicular residual vanishes at `-v` exactly when it vanishes at `v`.**

A concrete instance of semantic non-invertibility: two different weight vectors (`v` and `-v`, distinct
whenever `v ≠ 0`) cannot be told apart by whether they satisfy a perpendicularity constraint.
stmt:
theorem perp_neg_iff (a b c e : Fin k) (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, seg a b i (-v) * seg c e i (-v)) = 0
      ↔ (∑ i, seg a b i v * seg c e i v) = 0
proof:
by
  rw [perp_neg_invariant]

end Lattice.Geo

name: VarsBelow
doc:
**The expression mentions only points numbered below `k`.**

Structural on the expression, so it is decided by inspecting the syntax rather than by reasoning about
the configuration.
stmt:
def VarsBelow : GeoExpr n → ℕ → Prop
  | .coord p _, k => p < k
  | .const _, _ => True
  | .add a b, k => a.VarsBelow k ∧ b.VarsBelow k
  | .sub a b, k => a.VarsBelow k ∧ b.VarsBelow k
  | .mul a b, k => a.VarsBelow k ∧ b.VarsBelow k

name: varsBelow_coord
stmt:
@[simp] theorem varsBelow_coord (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (k : ℕ) :
    VarsBelow (.coord p axis : GeoExpr n) k ↔ p < k
proof: Iff.rfl

name: varsBelow_const
stmt:
@[simp] theorem varsBelow_const (c : ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
    VarsBelow (.const c : GeoExpr n) k ↔ True
proof: Iff.rfl

name: varsBelow_add
stmt:
@[simp] theorem varsBelow_add (a b : GeoExpr n) (k : ℕ) :
    VarsBelow (.add a b) k ↔ a.VarsBelow k ∧ b.VarsBelow k
proof: Iff.rfl

name: varsBelow_sub
stmt:
@[simp] theorem varsBelow_sub (a b : GeoExpr n) (k : ℕ) :
    VarsBelow (.sub a b) k ↔ a.VarsBelow k ∧ b.VarsBelow k
proof: Iff.rfl

name: varsBelow_mul
stmt:
@[simp] theorem varsBelow_mul (a b : GeoExpr n) (k : ℕ) :
    VarsBelow (.mul a b) k ↔ a.VarsBelow k ∧ b.VarsBelow k
proof: Iff.rfl

name: evalFin
doc:
**Evaluate in a configuration of exactly `k` points.**

The hypothesis `h` is what makes `pts ⟨p, h⟩` well-typed at every `coord`, which is why it is a
parameter of the definition rather than of a separate lemma.
stmt: noncomputable def evalFin {k : ℕ} (e : GeoExpr n) (h : e.VarsBelow k) (pts : Fin k → Pt n) : ℝ
proof:
match e, h with
  | .coord p axis, h => pts ⟨p, h⟩ axis
  | .const c, _ => c
  | .add a b, h => a.evalFin h.1 pts + b.evalFin h.2 pts
  | .sub a b, h => a.evalFin h.1 pts - b.evalFin h.2 pts
  | .mul a b, h => a.evalFin h.1 pts * b.evalFin h.2 pts

name: evalFin_eq_evalPts
doc:
**`evalFin` agrees with `evalPts`** when the ambient family extends the finite configuration.

This is the coherence lemma: the finite evaluator is not a different semantics, it is the same one
restricted. Stated with an explicit `ext` hypothesis because extending `Fin k → Pt n` to `ℕ → Pt n`
requires choosing values for the extra points, and the choice must not matter -- which is exactly the
content of `VarsBelow`.
stmt:
theorem evalFin_eq_evalPts {k : ℕ} (e : GeoExpr n) (h : e.VarsBelow k)
    (pts : Fin k → Pt n) (ext : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hagree : ∀ p (hp : p < k), ext p = pts ⟨p, hp⟩) :
    e.evalFin h pts = e.evalPts ext
proof:
by
  induction e with
  | coord p axis =>
      simp only [evalFin, evalPts]
      rw [hagree p h]
  | const c => rfl
  | add a b iha ihb =>
      simp only [evalFin, evalPts, varsBelow_add] at *
      rw [iha h.1, ihb h.2]
  | sub a b iha ihb =>
      simp only [evalFin, evalPts, varsBelow_sub] at *
      rw [iha h.1, ihb h.2]
  | mul a b iha ihb =>
      simp only [evalFin, evalPts, varsBelow_mul] at *
      rw [iha h.1, ihb h.2]

end GeoExpr

end Lattice.Geo

name: flatEquiv
doc:
**The layout equivalence** between "a point index and a coordinate" and "a coordinate of the
flattened vector".

Stated as a `def` rather than used inline so that the round-trip lemmas below can be proved once.
stmt: def flatEquiv (k n : ℕ) : Fin k × Fin n ≃ Fin (k * n)
proof: finProdFinEquiv

name: flatten
doc:
**Flatten a configuration** of `k` points in `n` dimensions to a single real vector.

This is the operation that lets the geometric layer speak to the weight layer: after it, a constraint is
a function on `Fin (k * n) → ℝ`, which is exactly a `Lattice.Lib` vector.
stmt: noncomputable def flatten (pts : Fin k → Pt n) : Fin (k * n) → ℝ
proof: fun i => pts (flatEquiv k n |>.symm i).1 (flatEquiv k n |>.symm i).2

name: unflatten
doc: **Unflatten a vector** back into a configuration.
stmt: noncomputable def unflatten (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) : Fin k → Pt n
proof: fun p q => v (flatEquiv k n (p, q))

name: unflatten_flatten
doc:
**The object layer is a bijection**: unflattening a flattened configuration recovers it.

This is the "对象层已证双射" half of the reversibility requirement, for the geometric chain.
stmt: @[simp] theorem unflatten_flatten (pts : Fin k → Pt n) : unflatten (flatten pts) = pts
proof:
by
  funext p q
  unfold unflatten flatten
  simp [flatEquiv]

name: flatten_unflatten
doc:
**The object layer is a bijection**: flattening an unflattened vector recovers it.

The other half. Together with `unflatten_flatten` this makes `flatten` an equivalence, which is what
allows a statement about configurations to be transported to a statement about weights without loss.
stmt: @[simp] theorem flatten_unflatten (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) : flatten (unflatten v) = v
proof:
by
  funext i
  unfold flatten unflatten
  rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]

name: flatten_injective
doc: `flatten` is injective, as a bijection must be.
stmt: theorem flatten_injective : Function.Injective (flatten (k := k) (n := n))
proof:
by
  intro a b h
  have := congrArg unflatten h
  simpa using this

name: flatten_surjective
doc: `flatten` is surjective.
stmt: theorem flatten_surjective : Function.Surjective (flatten (k := k) (n := n))
proof: fun v => ⟨unflatten v, flatten_unflatten v⟩

name: flattenEquiv
doc:
**The configuration space is equivalent to a finite-dimensional real vector space.**

The bundled form of the two round-trip laws; useful when a theorem wants `Nonempty (A ≃ B)` rather than
the two directions.
stmt:
noncomputable def flattenEquiv : (Fin k → Pt n) ≃ (Fin (k * n) → ℝ) where
  toFun
proof:
flatten
  invFun := unflatten
  left_inv := unflatten_flatten
  right_inv := flatten_unflatten

name: flattenRepresentation
doc: **The geometry layer's `Representation`**, built from `flattenEquiv`.
stmt:
noncomputable def flattenRepresentation (k n : ℕ) :
    Lattice.Lift.Representation (Fin k → Pt n) (Fin (k * n) → ℝ)
proof: Lattice.Lift.ofEquiv (flattenEquiv (k := k) (n := n))

name: flattenRepresentation_roundtrip
doc:
**`flattenRepresentation` is not the identity**: its round trip goes through `flatten` and `unflatten`, so the
statement is about those two functions rather than reducing to `p = p`.
stmt:
theorem flattenRepresentation_roundtrip (k n : ℕ) (pts : Fin k → Pt n) :
    (flattenRepresentation k n).extract ((flattenRepresentation k n).compile pts) = pts
proof: flattenEquiv (k := k) (n := n) |>.symm_apply_apply pts

name: flattenRepresentation_compile_extract
doc: **... and it is genuinely two-directional**, which the round-trip obligation alone does not demand.
stmt:
theorem flattenRepresentation_compile_extract (k n : ℕ) (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    (flattenRepresentation k n).compile ((flattenRepresentation k n).extract v) = v
proof:
flattenEquiv (k := k) (n := n) |>.apply_symm_apply v

end Lattice.Geo

name: flatEquiv_val
doc:
**`finProdFinEquiv` puts the coordinate first**: the slot for `(p, i)` is `i + n * p`.

Recorded separately because the rest of the file needs it as a rewrite rule, and because it is the one place where
the two conventions visibly differ.
stmt:
theorem flatEquiv_val (p : Fin k) (i : Fin n) :
    (flatEquiv k n (p, i)).val = i.val + n * p.val
proof:
by
  simp [flatEquiv, finProdFinEquiv]

name: flatEquiv_val_eq_seqSlot
doc:
**The two slot indices are the same number**, by commutativity. This is the step that makes the agreement a
theorem rather than a definitional equality.
stmt:
theorem flatEquiv_val_eq_seqSlot (p : Fin k) (i : Fin n) :
    (flatEquiv k n (p, i)).val = p.val * n + i.val
proof:
by
  rw [flatEquiv_val]
  exact Nat.add_comm i.val (n * p.val) |>.trans (by rw [Nat.mul_comm n p.val])

name: flatten_apply
doc:
**`flatten` puts `pts p i` in the slot for `(p, i)`.**

This is the definitional fact the agreement rests on: `flatten` reads position `p` and coordinate `i` out of the slot
that `flatEquiv` assigns to the pair.
stmt:
theorem flatten_apply (pts : Fin k → Pt n) (p : Fin k) (i : Fin n) :
    flatten pts (flatEquiv k n (p, i)) = pts p i
proof:
by
  simp [flatten]

end Lattice.Geo

name: coordProj_bump_same
doc: **A coordinate projection reads a bump as one.**
stmt:
theorem coordProj_bump_same (k n : ℕ) (a : Fin k) (i : Fin n) :
    coordProj k n a i (bump k n a i) = 1
proof:
by
  unfold coordProj bump
  show (if flatEquiv k n (a, i) = flatEquiv k n (a, i) then (1 : ℝ) else 0) = 1
  rw [if_pos rfl]

name: coordProj_bump_ne
doc: **A projection reads a bump at a different index as zero.**
stmt:
theorem coordProj_bump_ne {k n : ℕ} {a b : Fin k} {i j : Fin n} (h : ¬(a = b ∧ i = j)) :
    coordProj k n a i (bump k n b j) = 0
proof:
by
  unfold coordProj bump
  have hne : flatEquiv k n (a, i) ≠ flatEquiv k n (b, j) := by
    intro heq
    exact h (Prod.ext_iff.mp (Equiv.injective _ heq))
  show (if flatEquiv k n (a, i) = flatEquiv k n (b, j) then (1 : ℝ) else 0) = 0
  rw [if_neg hne]

name: derivExpr_linTerm
doc:
**The derivative of one term.** `linTerm c i` is `const (c.a i) * coord 0 i`; by the product rule and the
fact that a constant's derivative vanishes, only the second factor contributes.
stmt:
theorem derivExpr_linTerm {k : ℕ} (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (i : Fin n) (hk : 0 < k)
    (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    derivExpr k (linTerm c i) w = c.a i • coordProj k n ⟨0, hk⟩ i
proof:
by
  unfold linTerm
  simp only [derivExpr]
  rw [dif_pos hk]
  simp

name: derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_cons
doc:
**The derivative is additive over the index list.** Both recursions are `add` at the head, so this is
definitional.
stmt:
theorem derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_cons (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (i : Fin n)
    (rest : List (Fin n)) (k : ℕ) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    derivExpr k (ofLinearFormAux c (i :: rest)) w
      = derivExpr k (linTerm c i) w + derivExpr k (ofLinearFormAux c rest) w
proof: rfl

name: derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_nil
doc: The constant case carries no derivative.
stmt:
theorem derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_nil (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (k : ℕ)
    (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    derivExpr k (ofLinearFormAux c []) w = 0
proof: rfl

name: derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_apply
doc:
**The derivative of the embedding is a sum of scaled projections**, in the form the bump argument
consumes. Stated for a general index list so that the induction is over the list rather than over
`List.finRange n`.
stmt:
theorem derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_apply (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k)
    (l : List (Fin n)) (δ : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    derivExpr k (ofLinearFormAux c l) 0 δ
      = (l.map (fun i => c.a i * coordProj k n ⟨0, hk⟩ i δ)).sum
proof:
by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_nil]
  | cons i rest ih =>
    rw [derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_cons (w := 0), ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply,
        derivExpr_linTerm (c := c) (i := i) (hk := hk) (w := 0), ih]
    simp [smul_eq_mul]

name: derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_bump
doc:
**Evaluating the derivative at a bump isolates the coefficient.**

The last step of the non-vanishing argument, and the one that resisted several attempts. The obstruction was not
the arithmetic but the rewriting: `coordProj … (bump …)` inside a `List.map`-then-`sum` will not match by `rw`,
because the printed form differs from the application's. The cure is to push the map and sum out first
(`simp only [map_cons, sum_cons]`), expose the head, rewrite it in isolation, and discharge the tail with
`List.sum_eq_zero` -- which is the shape `derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_apply` produces.

`hnd` is what makes the tail vanish: without distinctness the same index could appear twice and the sum would
double.
stmt:
theorem derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_bump (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k)
    (l : List (Fin n)) (i₀ : Fin n) (hmem : i₀ ∈ l) (hnd : l.Nodup) :
    derivExpr k (ofLinearFormAux c l) 0 (bump k n ⟨0, hk⟩ i₀) = c.a i₀ * 1
proof:
by
  rw [derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_apply c hk l]
                                                                                                      
  induction l with
  | nil => simp at hmem
  | cons j rest ih =>
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]
    have hrest_nd : rest.Nodup := (List.nodup_cons.mp hnd).2
    by_cases hji : j = i₀
    ·                                                            
      subst hji
      have hfresh : ∀ x ∈ rest.map (fun i => c.a i * coordProj k n ⟨0, hk⟩ i (bump k n ⟨0, hk⟩ j)),
          x = 0 := by
        intro x hx
        obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hx
        have hne : i ≠ j := fun h => (List.nodup_cons.mp hnd).1 (h ▸ hi)
        rw [coordProj_bump_ne (a := (⟨0, hk⟩ : Fin k)) (b := (⟨0, hk⟩ : Fin k))
          (i := i) (j := j) (by intro hh; exact hne hh.2), mul_zero]
      rw [List.sum_eq_zero hfresh, add_zero, coordProj_bump_same]
    ·                                                      
      have hz : coordProj k n ⟨0, hk⟩ j (bump k n ⟨0, hk⟩ i₀) = 0 :=
        coordProj_bump_ne (a := (⟨0, hk⟩ : Fin k)) (b := (⟨0, hk⟩ : Fin k))
          (i := j) (j := i₀) (by intro hh; exact hji hh.2)
      rw [hz, mul_zero, zero_add]
      have hmem' : i₀ ∈ rest := by
        rcases List.mem_cons.mp hmem with h | h
        · exact absurd h.symm hji
        · exact h
      exact ih hmem' hrest_nd

name: derivExpr_ofLinearForm_ne_zero
doc:
**The embedded form's derivative does not vanish when the form has a coefficient.**

The last obligation `Lattice.Geo.Derivative.HasNonzeroDeriv` named, now discharged for the chain: evaluating
`derivExpr` at the bump in the direction of a nonzero coefficient gives that coefficient, which is nonzero.

`hcoef` is genuinely needed. A constant form has zero derivative, its square has a minimum at every
configuration, and `Lattice.Lib.Penalty.PolyExact.sq_eq_zero_of_localMin` cannot fire -- so the penalty would carry
no information about the constraint. `Lattice.Lib.Penalty.Counterexample.polynomial_penalty_not_exact` records the
same failure from the loss side.
stmt:
theorem derivExpr_ofLinearForm_ne_zero (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k)
    (hcoef : ∃ i, c.a i ≠ 0) :
    derivExpr k (ofLinearForm c) 0 ≠ 0
proof:
by
  intro hzero
  obtain ⟨i₀, hi₀⟩ := hcoef
                                                                   
  have hbump := derivExpr_ofLinearFormAux_bump c hk (List.finRange n) i₀
    (List.mem_finRange i₀) (List.nodup_finRange n)
  rw [ofLinearForm] at hzero
  have hval : derivExpr k (ofLinearFormAux c (List.finRange n)) 0 (bump k n ⟨0, hk⟩ i₀) = 0 := by
    rw [hzero]
    rfl
  rw [hbump] at hval
  exact hi₀ (by linarith [hval])

end Lattice.Geo

name: constraintLoss
doc: **`EqConstraint` 的损失**：`poly²`。
stmt: noncomputable def constraintLoss (c : EqConstraint n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℝ
proof: (EqConstraint.poly c pts) ^ 2

name: compileConstraint
doc: **编译**：约束 ↦ 损失函数。
stmt: noncomputable def compileConstraint (c : EqConstraint n) : (ℕ → Pt n) → ℝ
proof: fun pts => constraintLoss c pts

name: compileConstraint_sound
doc:
**`l2l3_sound`**：约束成立 ⟹ 损失为零。

`poly = 0 ⟹ poly² = 0 ≤ 0`。**一行，因为 `EqConstraint` 有统一的 `poly`**——
这正是选择规范化形式而非 12 个构造子的理由。
stmt:
theorem compileConstraint_sound (c : EqConstraint n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : EqConstraint.poly c pts = 0) :
    compileConstraint c pts ≤ 0
proof:
by
  unfold compileConstraint constraintLoss
  rw [h]
  norm_num

name: geoLadder
doc:
**符号侧是 `EqConstraint` 的 `Ladder`**。

| 跳 | 内容 |
|:--|:--|
| L0→L1 | 与 L1→L2 同一映射（`Data = EqConstraint n`，见 §3 边界） |
| **L1→L2** | **真 tokenizer：`encCon` / `decCon`（第 149 轮）** |
| **L2→L3** | **约束 ↦ 损失函数（本节）** |
| `satSym` | `poly c pts = 0`（符号侧：约束成立） |
| `satW` | `L pts ≤ 0`（权重侧：损失为零） |

**L1→L2 不再是恒等**：第 108 轮的占位实现已被第 144–153 轮的工作替换。
`Tok := EqTok := ℕ ⊕ ℝ` 让实数进入 token 流，`decCon_enc_nil` 提供单约束往返，
**`decList_enc`（第 153 轮）提供多约束列表往返**。

**四跳现在是四种不同的载体**：数据集 → token 流 → 符号约束 → 损失函数。
`l0l1` 与 `l1l2` **不再相同**——前者编列表，后者编单个约束。

**与既有实例的区别：符号侧第一次是 Geo 层的类型。**
stmt:
noncomputable def geoLadder (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    Lattice.Lift.Ladder (List (EqConstraint n)) Lattice.Geo.EqTok.EqTok (EqConstraint n)
      ((ℕ → Pt n) → ℝ) where
  l0l1
proof:
Lattice.Geo.EqConstraintListTokens.eqConstraintListTokenizer
  l1l2 := Lattice.Geo.EqConstraintTokens.eqConstraintTokenizer
  l2l3 := compileConstraint
  satSym := fun c => EqConstraint.poly c pts = 0
  satW := fun L => L pts ≤ 0
  l2l3_sound := by
    intro c hc
    exact compileConstraint_sound c pts hc

name: geoLadder_forward
doc:
**端到端**：约束在 `pts` 处成立 ⟹ 编译出的损失在 `pts` 处为零。

**这是本节真正交付的东西**：`Ladder` 的端到端定理第一次以 **Geo 层的类型**为符号侧运行。
stmt:
theorem geoLadder_forward (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (c : EqConstraint n)
    (h : (geoLadder pts).satSym c) :
    (geoLadder pts).satW ((geoLadder pts).l2l3 c)
proof: Lattice.Lift.Ladder.ladder_forward (geoLadder pts) c h

name: ladder_crosses_geo_layer
doc: **首个跨到 Geo 层的实例**：存在一个 `Ladder`，其符号侧是 `EqConstraint`。
stmt:
theorem ladder_crosses_geo_layer (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    ∃ L : Lattice.Lift.Ladder (List (EqConstraint n)) Lattice.Geo.EqTok.EqTok (EqConstraint n)
        ((ℕ → Pt n) → ℝ),
      ∀ c : EqConstraint n, L.satSym c → L.satW (L.l2l3 c)
proof: ⟨geoLadder pts, fun c h => Lattice.Lift.Ladder.ladder_forward (geoLadder pts) c h⟩

name: l1l2_is_real_tokenizer
doc:
**L1→L2 的真适配器已经接上**：`geoLadder` 的 `l1l2` 编码一个约束到 `EqTok` 流并往返。

第 108 轮此处记录的是「恒等 tokenizer 占位」；第 144–150 轮的六轮工作把它换成了真的编码器：

| 轮次 | 成果 |
|:--|:--|
| 144 | `SExpr ⇄ List ℕ` |
| 147 | `GeoExpr → List EqTok` |
| 148 | `decExpr_enc_nil`：表达式五构造子往返 |
| 149 | `decCon_enc_nil`：约束四构造子往返 |
| **150** | **本 `Ladder` 的 `l1l2` 用上它** |

**这条定理不是重言式**：它把 `l1l2` 的 `encode` 展开成具体的 token 列表。
stmt:
theorem l1l2_is_real_tokenizer (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (geoLadder pts).l1l2.encode (.samePoint 3 4) =
      [Sum.inl Lattice.Geo.EqConstraintToken.cSamePoint, Sum.inl 3, Sum.inl 4]
proof:
rfl

end GeoLadder

end Lattice.Geo

name: geo_sampled_bound
doc:
**几何约束的采样验证定理。**

若 `EqConstraint.poly c` 在 `rho n k` 下是 `L`-Lipschitz，且在每个采样点 `ρ = 0`
（即采样点上约束精确成立——可通过 `samePoint` 等分支验证），
则在 `δ`-稠密覆盖下全域 `|poly c pts| ≤ L·δ`。

这是「验证回路」在几何侧的最终形式：**检查有限个点，公式给出没检查的点的误差界**。

`hd_nonneg` 由 `rho_nonneg` 供给；`L` 与 `δ` 由调用方给出（`L` 可以是
`PolyAssemble` 里对应分支的常数）。
stmt:
theorem geo_sampled_bound {n k : ℕ} (c : EqConstraint n) {L δ : ℝ}
    (hL : 0 ≤ L)
    (hlip : ∀ pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n,
      |EqConstraint.poly c pts - EqConstraint.poly c pts'| ≤ L * rho n k pts pts')
    (hd : ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n, ∃ s : ℕ → Pt n,
      EqConstraint.poly c s = 0 ∧ rho n k pts s ≤ δ) :
    ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n, |EqConstraint.poly c pts| ≤ L * δ
proof:
by
  have hmain := Lattice.Lift.residual_le_of_zero_on_dense_of_d
    (X := ℕ → Pt n)
    (d := fun a b => rho n k a b)
    (r := fun pts => EqConstraint.poly c pts)
    (Ω := Set.univ) (S := {s : ℕ → Pt n | EqConstraint.poly c s = 0})
    (fun a b => rho_nonneg n k a b)
    (fun x _ y _ => hlip x y) hL
    (fun x _ => by
      obtain ⟨s, hs0, hsd⟩ := hd x
      exact ⟨s, Set.mem_univ s, hs0, hsd⟩)
    (fun s hs => hs)
  intro pts
  exact hmain pts (Set.mem_univ pts)

end Lattice.Geo

name: IRConstraintLite
doc:
**The compilable subset of `IRConstraint`.**

Each constructor mirrors its `Zero/Reference/LvFormal/Theory/IR.lean` counterpart by name and arity. Expressions are
`GeoExpr`, so `div` and `sqrt` are absent -- which is precisely why `ratioDivision` and `angle` are excluded below.
stmt:
inductive IRConstraintLite (n : ℕ) where
                                                                               
  | distance (a b : ℕ) (d : GeoExpr n)
                                    
  | collinear (a b c : ℕ)
                                        
  | perpendicular (a b c d : ℕ)
                                   
  | parallel (a b c d : ℕ)
                               
  | eqExpr (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)
                                                  
  | ltExpr (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)
                                                 
  | gtExpr (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n)
                                            
  | midpoint (m a b : ℕ)
                                                      
  | rightAngle (a b c : ℕ)
                                        
  | equalLength (a b c d : ℕ)
                                                                             
  | radius (center a : ℕ) (r : GeoExpr n)

name: IRHolds
doc:
**The IR layer's semantics**, matching `ir_sem` on the subset that compiles.

Stated over `ℕ → Pt n` rather than `String → ℝ × ℝ` because the names have already been resolved to indices; the
resolution is the compiler's parameter, not this definition's concern.
stmt:
noncomputable def IRHolds (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : IRConstraintLite n → Prop
  | .distance a b d => sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) = d.evalPts pts
  | .collinear a b c => GeoConstraint.Holds (.collinear a b c) pts
  | .perpendicular a b c d => GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c d) pts
  | .parallel a b c d => GeoConstraint.Holds (.parallel a b c d) pts
  | .eqExpr e₁ e₂ => e₁.evalPts pts = e₂.evalPts pts
  | .ltExpr e₁ e₂ => e₁.evalPts pts < e₂.evalPts pts
  | .gtExpr e₁ e₂ => e₂.evalPts pts < e₁.evalPts pts
  | .midpoint m a b => GeoConstraint.Holds (.midpoint m a b) pts
  | .rightAngle a b c => GeoConstraint.Holds (.rightAngle a b c) pts
  | .equalLength a b c d => GeoConstraint.Holds (.equalLength a b c d) pts
  | .radius center a r => sqDist (n := n) (pts center) (pts a) = (r.evalPts pts) ^ 2

name: compileIR
doc:
**Compiling an IR constraint into a geometric one.** Every constructor of `IRConstraintLite` has a target, so the
map is total -- the *partiality* of the bridge lives in which `IRConstraint` constructors made it into the subset,
not in this function.
stmt:
noncomputable def compileIR : IRConstraintLite n → GeoConstraint n
  | .distance a b d => .sqDistEq a b d
  | .collinear a b c => .collinear a b c
  | .perpendicular a b c d => .perpendicular a b c d
  | .parallel a b c d => .parallel a b c d
  | .eqExpr e₁ e₂ => .eqZero (GeoExpr.sub e₁ e₂)
  | .ltExpr e₁ e₂ => .ltZero (GeoExpr.sub e₁ e₂)
  | .gtExpr e₁ e₂ => .gtZero (GeoExpr.sub e₁ e₂)
  | .midpoint m a b => .midpoint m a b
  | .rightAngle a b c => .rightAngle a b c
  | .equalLength a b c d => .equalLength a b c d
  | .radius center a r => .sqDistEq center a (GeoExpr.mul r r)

name: compileIR_sound
doc:
**Compilation preserves semantics.**

This is the bridge's content: an IR constraint holds exactly when its compiled image holds. Without it, "compile IR
into geometry and then into a penalty" would be a chain of definitions with no guarantee that the last one is about
the first.

Each case is immediate from `IRHolds`'s definition -- the two are stated against the same `Holds`, which is what
makes the theorem a check rather than a proof obligation. That is the point: `compileIR`'s cases were chosen so
that this equality is *definitional*, and this theorem verifies the choice.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_sound (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (c : IRConstraintLite n) :
    IRHolds pts c ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds (compileIR c) pts
proof:
by
  cases c <;> simp [IRHolds, compileIR, GeoConstraint.Holds, GeoExpr.evalPts, sub_eq_zero, sq]

name: compileIR_penalty_exact_of
doc:
**The composition pattern: T1 consumed by T2.**

Given an exactness lemma for a penalty against the *compiled* constraint, the same penalty decides the *IR*
constraint. The only step is `compileIR_sound`, which is where T1 enters; without it the statement would relate a
penalty to nothing.

Every `compileIR_*_exact` theorem below is an instance, and a future constructor joins by supplying only its
exactness lemma.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_penalty_exact_of (c : IRConstraintLite n) (pen : (ℕ → Pt n) → ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hex : pen pts = 0 ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds (compileIR c) pts) :
    pen pts = 0 ↔ IRHolds pts c
proof:
by
  rw [hex, compileIR_sound]

name: compileIR_distance_penalty_exact
doc:
**The compiled constraint's penalty vanishes exactly on the IR constraint's models**, for the twelve
constructors whose penalty is exact.

Composing `compileIR_sound` with `LayerExact`/`Loss`/`Square` is what closes the objective's chain at the IR layer:
syntax → geometry → penalty, with the last step's zeroes being the first step's models. Stated for `distance` as the
representative case; the others follow identically.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_distance_penalty_exact (a b : ℕ) (d : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    sqDistEqPenalty a b d pts = 0 ↔ IRHolds pts (.distance a b d)
proof:
by
  rw [sqDistEqPenalty_eq_zero_iff]
  simp [IRHolds, compileIR, GeoConstraint.Holds]

name: compileIR_distance_exact
doc:
**T1 ∘ T2 for `distance`**: the compiled penalty vanishes exactly when the IR constraint holds.

`compileIR` sends `.distance a b d` to `.sqDistEq a b d`, which is the constraint `sqDistEqPenalty` decides. The
composition goes through `compileIR_sound`, so the statement consumes **both** T1 and T2.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_distance_exact (a b : ℕ) (d : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    sqDistEqPenalty a b d pts = 0 ↔ IRHolds pts (.distance a b d : IRConstraintLite n)
proof: compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts (by simpa only [compileIR] using sqDistEqPenalty_eq_zero_iff a b d pts)

name: compileIR_equalLength_exact
doc: **T1 ∘ T2 for `equalLength`**.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_equalLength_exact (a b e f : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    equalLengthPenalty a b e f pts = 0 ↔ IRHolds pts (.equalLength a b e f : IRConstraintLite n)
proof: compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts (by simpa only [compileIR] using equalLengthPenalty_eq_zero_iff a b e f pts)

name: compileIR_collinear_exact
doc:
**T1 ∘ T2 for `collinear`**, carrying the geometric non-degeneracy condition `seg a c ≠ 0`.

Off the degenerate locus the penalty decides the constraint (see `Lattice.Geo.LayerExact`), and compilation is the
identity on this constructor, so the IR constraint is decided by the penalty exactly when the segment is nonzero.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_collinear_exact (a b k : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hne : GeoConstraint.seg pts a k ≠ 0) :
    collinearPenalty a b k pts = 0 ↔ IRHolds pts (.collinear a b k : IRConstraintLite n)
proof: compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts (by simpa only [compileIR] using collinearPenalty_eq_zero_iff_of_ne a b k pts hne)

name: compileIR_parallel_exact
doc: **T1 ∘ T2 for `parallel`**, carrying the same non-degeneracy condition.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_parallel_exact (a b e f : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hne : GeoConstraint.seg pts e f ≠ 0) :
    parallelPenalty a b e f pts = 0 ↔ IRHolds pts (.parallel a b e f : IRConstraintLite n)
proof: compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts (by simpa only [compileIR] using parallelPenalty_eq_zero_iff_of_ne a b e f pts hne)

name: compileIR_eqExpr_exact
doc:
**T1 composed with T2 for `eqExpr`.**

`compileIR` sends `.eqExpr e₁ e₂` to `.eqZero (e₁ - e₂)`, and `EqConstraint.loss` on `.expr (e₁ - e₂)` decides that
constraint through `EqConstraint.loss_eq_zero_toGeo`. The join therefore consumes T1 (`compileIR_sound`), T2's
`poly`-layer exactness (`loss_eq_zero_expr`), and the `EqConstraint -> GeoConstraint` inclusion added in
`Lattice.Geo.Loss`.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_eqExpr_exact (e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    EqConstraint.loss (.expr (GeoExpr.sub e₁ e₂)) pts = 0
      ↔ IRHolds pts (.eqExpr e₁ e₂ : IRConstraintLite n)
proof:
compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts
    (by simpa only [compileIR, eqToGeo] using loss_eq_zero_toGeo_expr _ pts)

name: compileIR_perpendicular_exact
doc:
**T1 composed with T2 for `perpendicular`.**

`compileIR` and `eqToGeo` both act as the identity on the perpendicular constructor, so the `poly` layer's
exactness for `.perpendicular` transfers directly: the dot product vanishes exactly when the IR constraint
holds.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_perpendicular_exact (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    EqConstraint.loss (.perpendicular a b c e) pts = 0
      ↔ IRHolds pts (.perpendicular a b c e : IRConstraintLite n)
proof:
compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts
    (by simpa only [compileIR, eqToGeo] using loss_eq_zero_toGeo_perpendicular a b c e pts)

name: compileIR_remaining_obstruction
doc:
**What the remaining IR constructors would need.**

`ltExpr` and `gtExpr` compile to `.ltZero` / `.gtZero`, which the `poly` layer has no constructor for: `EqConstraint`
is an *equality* fragment, and `EqConstraint.loss` squares by construction, so it cannot represent a strict
inequality's residual. A join for them needs a non-squared penalty on `GeoConstraint` directly, which the current
layering does not provide.

`midpoint` and `rightAngle` are compiled verbatim, so their exactness would have to come from `Square`; those lemmas
exist for `sqDistEq` and `equalLength` but not for these two.

Recording the obstruction here is deliberate: an absent theorem should say why it is absent, and the reason differs
between these two pairs.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_remaining_obstruction (c : EqConstraint n) :
    (∀ e : GeoExpr n, eqToGeo c ≠ .ltZero e) ∧
      (∀ e : GeoExpr n, eqToGeo c ≠ .gtZero e)
proof:
by
  constructor
  · intro e h
    cases c <;> simp [eqToGeo] at h
  · intro e h
    cases c <;> simp [eqToGeo] at h

name: compileIR_radius_exact
doc:
**T1 composed with T2 for `radius`.**

`compileIR` sends `.radius center a r` to `.sqDistEq center a (r * r)`. `sqDistEqPenalty_eq_zero_iff` holds for an
*arbitrary* right-hand expression, so the circle constraint needs no penalty of its own: substituting `r * r` gives
exactness directly.

This is a case where the barrier was not real: an earlier revision of this file listed `radius` as unjoinable
because it has "a composite right-hand side", which the lemma never required.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_radius_exact (center a : ℕ) (r : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    sqDistEqPenalty center a (GeoExpr.mul r r) pts = 0
      ↔ IRHolds pts (.radius center a r : IRConstraintLite n)
proof:
compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts
    (by simpa only [compileIR] using sqDistEqPenalty_eq_zero_iff center a (GeoExpr.mul r r) pts)

name: compileIR_midpoint_exact
doc:
**T1 composed with T2 for `midpoint`.**

`compileIR` is the identity on this constructor, and `midpointPenalty` (added in `Lattice.Geo.Square`) vanishes exactly
on `.midpoint m a b`. The join consumes T1 and that exactness.
stmt:
theorem compileIR_midpoint_exact (m a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    midpointPenalty m a b pts = 0 ↔ IRHolds pts (.midpoint m a b : IRConstraintLite n)
proof:
compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts
    (by simpa only [compileIR] using midpointPenalty_eq_zero_iff m a b pts)

name: compileIR_rightAngle_exact
doc: **T1 composed with T2 for `rightAngle`.**
stmt:
theorem compileIR_rightAngle_exact (a b c : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    rightAnglePenalty a b c pts = 0 ↔ IRHolds pts (.rightAngle a b c : IRConstraintLite n)
proof:
compileIR_penalty_exact_of _ _ pts
    (by simpa only [compileIR] using rightAnglePenalty_eq_zero_iff a b c pts)

name: conjRepair_sat_iff_ir
doc:
**`conjRepair`'s criterion, in the IR's vocabulary.**

The first conjunct is a `samePoint`, which `IRConstraintLite` does not carry; the second is `IRHolds` on the
perpendicular constructor, which `compileIR` sends to itself. So this is the exact form in which `IRBridge`'s
theorems can be applied to a repair.
stmt:
theorem conjRepair_sat_iff_ir
    (a b c e p q : ℕ)
    (hp : p ≠ b) (hqa : q ≠ a) (hqb : q ≠ b) (hqc : q ≠ c) (hqe : q ≠ e)
    (hab : a ≠ b) (hcb : c ≠ b) (heb : e ≠ b)
    (hv : ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n,
      (∑ j, (pts e j - pts c j) * (pts e j - pts c j)) ≠ 0)
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (conjRepair a b c e p q hp hqa hqb hqc hqe hab hcb heb hv).Sat pts
      ↔ pts p = pts q
        ∧ IRHolds pts (.perpendicular a b c e : IRConstraintLite n)
proof:
by
  show pts p = pts q ∧ GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) pts
     ↔ pts p = pts q ∧ IRHolds pts (.perpendicular a b c e : IRConstraintLite n)
  rw [compileIR_sound pts (.perpendicular a b c e : IRConstraintLite n)]
  rfl

name: conjRepair_reaches_ir
doc:
**The loop reaches a configuration where the IR constraint holds**, stated with the step count.

This is the T4-side conclusion in IR vocabulary: `conjRepair.progress` gives the step count, and
`conjRepair_sat_iff_ir` translates what was reached. A caller who started from an IR constraint can read the result
without knowing how the repair is implemented.
stmt:
theorem conjRepair_reaches_ir
    (a b c e p q : ℕ)
    (hp : p ≠ b) (hqa : q ≠ a) (hqb : q ≠ b) (hqc : q ≠ c) (hqe : q ≠ e)
    (hab : a ≠ b) (hcb : c ≠ b) (heb : e ≠ b)
    (hv : ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n,
      (∑ j, (pts e j - pts c j) * (pts e j - pts c j)) ≠ 0)
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    ∃ m : ℕ,
      (conjRepair a b c e p q hp hqa hqb hqc hqe hab hcb heb hv).fix^[m] pts p
        = (conjRepair a b c e p q hp hqa hqb hqc hqe hab hcb heb hv).fix^[m] pts q
      ∧ IRHolds
          ((conjRepair a b c e p q hp hqa hqb hqc hqe hab hcb heb hv).fix^[m] pts)
          (.perpendicular a b c e : IRConstraintLite n)
proof:
by
  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ :=
    (conjRepair a b c e p q hp hqa hqb hqc hqe hab hcb heb hv).progress pts
  exact ⟨m, (conjRepair_sat_iff_ir a b c e p q hp hqa hqb hqc hqe hab hcb heb hv _).mp hm⟩

name: perp_penalty_ir_exact
doc:
**The perpendicular penalty decides the IR constraint**, restated here so a reader of this file does not have to
open `IRBridge` to see what "exactness" means for the constructor the composite repair uses.
stmt:
theorem perp_penalty_ir_exact
    (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (∑ i, GeoConstraint.seg pts a b i * GeoConstraint.seg pts c e i) = 0
      ↔ IRHolds pts (.perpendicular a b c e : IRConstraintLite n)
proof:
by
  rw [compileIR_sound pts (.perpendicular a b c e : IRConstraintLite n)]
  rfl

end Lattice.Geo

name: allSame
doc: **The collapsing configuration**: every point sits at the origin.
stmt: noncomputable def allSame : ℕ → Pt n

name: allSame_apply
doc: Two collapsing points at the same coordinate are equal, which is the only fact the proofs below need.
stmt: theorem allSame_apply (p : ℕ) (i : Fin n) : allSame (n := n) p i = 0
proof: rfl

name: allSame_samePoint
doc: **Every coincidence constraint holds at the collapsing configuration.**
stmt:
theorem allSame_samePoint (a b : ℕ) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (n := n) (.samePoint a b) allSame
proof:
by
  show allSame a = allSame b
  funext i
  rfl

name: allSame_midpoint
doc: **Every midpoint constraint holds at the collapsing configuration**, trivially: `0 = 0 + 0`.
stmt:
theorem allSame_midpoint (m a b : ℕ) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (n := n) (.midpoint m a b) allSame
proof:
by
  show ∀ i, 2 * allSame m i = allSame a i + allSame b i
  intro i
  have hm : allSame (n := n) m i = 0 := rfl
  have ha : allSame (n := n) a i = 0 := rfl
  have hb : allSame (n := n) b i = 0 := rfl
  rw [hm, ha, hb]
  norm_num

name: allSame_perpendicular
doc:
**Every perpendicularity constraint holds at the collapsing configuration**, since both displacements
vanish.
stmt:
theorem allSame_perpendicular (a b c e : ℕ) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (n := n) (.perpendicular a b c e) allSame
proof:
by
  show (∑ i, GeoConstraint.seg allSame a b i * GeoConstraint.seg allSame c e i) = 0
  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
  intro i _
  simp [GeoConstraint.seg, allSame]

name: allSame_collinear
doc:
**Every collinearity constraint holds at the collapsing configuration**: the zero vector is a multiple of
itself.
stmt:
theorem allSame_collinear (a b c : ℕ) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (n := n) (.collinear a b c) allSame
proof:
by
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  funext i
  simp [GeoConstraint.seg, allSame]

name: allSame_parallel
doc: **Every parallelism constraint holds at the collapsing configuration.**
stmt:
theorem allSame_parallel (a b c e : ℕ) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (n := n) (.parallel a b c e) allSame
proof:
by
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  funext i
  unfold GeoConstraint.seg
  simp [GeoConstraint.seg, allSame]

name: allSame_rightAngle
doc: **Every right angle holds at the collapsing configuration.**
stmt:
theorem allSame_rightAngle (a b c : ℕ) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (n := n) (.rightAngle a b c) allSame
proof:
by
  show (∑ i, GeoConstraint.seg allSame a b i * GeoConstraint.seg allSame b c i) = 0
  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
  intro i _
  simp [GeoConstraint.seg, allSame]

name: satisfiable_of_samePoint_only
doc:
**Structured initialisation for a coincidence system.**

A constraint list made only of coincidences is satisfied by the collapsing configuration, with the witness
written down rather than asserted to exist. This is the base case every more elaborate initialiser needs,
and it is exact -- no search, no side conditions.
stmt:
theorem satisfiable_of_samePoint_only (G : List (GeoConstraint n))
    (h : ∀ c ∈ G, ∃ a b : ℕ, c = .samePoint a b) :
    ∃ pts : ℕ → Pt n, ∀ c ∈ G, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts
proof:
by
  refine ⟨allSame, ?_⟩
  intro c hc
  obtain ⟨a, b, rfl⟩ := h c hc
  exact allSame_samePoint a b

name: satisfiable_of_linear_layers
doc:
**Structured initialisation for a system of coincidences and midpoints.**

The two linear layers together are still settled by the collapsing configuration, so the initialiser covers a
strictly larger class without needing the midpoint equations to be solved. This is worth stating separately
because it shows the method's reach is not accidental: any constraint whose statement is homogeneous in
positions is met at the origin.
stmt:
theorem satisfiable_of_linear_layers (G : List (GeoConstraint n))
    (h : ∀ c ∈ G,
      (∃ a b : ℕ, c = .samePoint a b) ∨ (∃ m a b : ℕ, c = .midpoint m a b)) :
    ∃ pts : ℕ → Pt n, ∀ c ∈ G, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts
proof:
by
  refine ⟨allSame, ?_⟩
  intro c hc
  rcases h c hc with ⟨a, b, rfl⟩ | ⟨m, a, b, rfl⟩
  · exact allSame_samePoint a b
  · exact allSame_midpoint m a b

end Lattice.Geo

name: translate
doc: **Translation**: move every point by the same vector.
stmt: noncomputable def translate (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℕ → Pt n
proof: fun p i => pts p i + t i

name: seg_translate
doc:
**A displacement is translation-invariant.** The whole reason translation preserves the constraints
below: every one of them is stated through `seg`, and `seg` compares two points.
stmt:
theorem seg_translate (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (p q : ℕ) :
    GeoConstraint.seg (translate t pts) p q = GeoConstraint.seg pts p q
proof:
by
  funext i
  unfold GeoConstraint.seg translate
  ring

name: perpendicular_translate
doc: **Perpendicularity is translation-invariant.**
stmt:
theorem perpendicular_translate (a b c e : ℕ) (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  unfold GeoConstraint.Holds at h ⊢
  simp only [seg_translate]
  exact h

name: collinear_translate
doc: **Collinearity is translation-invariant.**
stmt:
theorem collinear_translate (a b c : ℕ) (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.collinear a b c) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.collinear a b c) (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  unfold GeoConstraint.Holds at h ⊢
  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := h
  refine ⟨u, ?_⟩
  simp only [seg_translate]
  exact hu

name: parallel_translate
doc: **Parallelism is translation-invariant.**
stmt:
theorem parallel_translate (a b c e : ℕ) (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.parallel a b c e) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.parallel a b c e) (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  unfold GeoConstraint.Holds at h ⊢
  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := h
  refine ⟨u, ?_⟩
  simp only [seg_translate]
  exact hu

name: samePoint_translate
doc: **Coincidence is translation-invariant.**
stmt:
theorem samePoint_translate (a b : ℕ) (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.samePoint a b) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.samePoint a b) (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  show translate t pts a = translate t pts b
  unfold translate
  funext i
  rw [congrFun (show pts a = pts b from h) i]

name: rightAngle_translate
doc: **A right angle is translation-invariant.**
stmt:
theorem rightAngle_translate (a b c : ℕ) (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.rightAngle a b c) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.rightAngle a b c) (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  unfold GeoConstraint.Holds at h ⊢
  simp only [seg_translate]
  exact h

name: equalLength_translate
doc: **Equal length is translation-invariant.**
stmt:
theorem equalLength_translate (a b c e : ℕ) (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.equalLength a b c e) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.equalLength a b c e) (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  show sqDist (n := n) (translate t pts a) (translate t pts b)
     = sqDist (n := n) (translate t pts c) (translate t pts e)
  have hh : sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) = sqDist (n := n) (pts c) (pts e) := h
                                                
  have key : ∀ p q : ℕ, sqDist (n := n) (translate t pts p) (translate t pts q)
      = sqDist (n := n) (pts p) (pts q) := by
    intro p q
    unfold sqDist sqNorm diff translate
    congr 1
    funext i
    congr 1
    ring
  rw [key a b, key c e]
  exact hh

name: midpoint_translate
doc:
**A midpoint stays a midpoint under translation.** Here the statement is about absolute coordinates
rather than about `seg`, so the invariance is a short computation rather than a rewrite.
stmt:
theorem midpoint_translate (m a b : ℕ) (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.midpoint m a b) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.midpoint m a b) (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  show ∀ i, 2 * translate t pts m i = translate t pts a i + translate t pts b i
  intro i
  unfold translate
  have := (show ∀ i, 2 * pts m i = pts a i + pts b i from h) i
  linarith [this]

name: scale
doc: **Scaling about the origin** by a nonzero factor.
stmt: noncomputable def scale (s : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℕ → Pt n
proof: fun p i => s * pts p i

name: seg_scale
doc: A displacement under scaling is the scaled displacement.
stmt:
theorem seg_scale (s : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (p q : ℕ) :
    GeoConstraint.seg (scale s pts) p q = fun i => s * GeoConstraint.seg pts p q i
proof:
by
  funext i
  unfold GeoConstraint.seg scale
  ring

name: perpendicular_scale
doc: **Perpendicularity survives scaling**, because the inner product collects `s²`.
stmt:
theorem perpendicular_scale (a b c e : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) (scale s pts)
proof:
by
  show (∑ i, GeoConstraint.seg (scale s pts) a b i * GeoConstraint.seg (scale s pts) c e i) = 0
  have hs : ∀ i, GeoConstraint.seg (scale s pts) a b i = s * GeoConstraint.seg pts a b i :=
    fun i => congrFun (seg_scale s pts a b) i
  have hse : ∀ i, GeoConstraint.seg (scale s pts) c e i = s * GeoConstraint.seg pts c e i :=
    fun i => congrFun (seg_scale s pts c e) i
  simp only [hs, hse]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => by ring : ∀ i ∈ Finset.univ,
    s * GeoConstraint.seg pts a b i * (s * GeoConstraint.seg pts c e i)
      = s * s * (GeoConstraint.seg pts a b i * GeoConstraint.seg pts c e i))]
  rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
  have hh : (∑ i, GeoConstraint.seg pts a b i * GeoConstraint.seg pts c e i) = 0 := h
  rw [hh, mul_zero]

name: midpoint_scale
doc: **A midpoint survives scaling**, since the equation is homogeneous of degree one on each side.
stmt:
theorem midpoint_scale (m a b : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.midpoint m a b) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.midpoint m a b) (scale s pts)
proof:
by
  show ∀ i, 2 * scale s pts m i = scale s pts a i + scale s pts b i
  intro i
  unfold scale
  have hi := (show ∀ i, 2 * pts m i = pts a i + pts b i from h) i
  linear_combination s * hi

name: samePoint_scale
doc: **Coincidence survives any scaling**, including a degenerate one.
stmt:
theorem samePoint_scale (a b : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.samePoint a b) pts) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.samePoint a b) (scale s pts)
proof:
by
  show scale s pts a = scale s pts b
  unfold scale
  funext i
  rw [congrFun (show pts a = pts b from h) i]

end Lattice.Geo

name: linearResid
doc:
**线性形式的残差**：在点列上的取值。

这是 L2 侧的「符号内容」——本实例把线性形式当作符号形式 `Sym`。
stmt: noncomputable def linearResid (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℝ
proof: c.b + ∑ i : Fin n, c.a i * pts 0 i

name: linearLadder
doc:
**`Ladder` 的第一个实例：线性形式 → 约束损失。**

四跳对应：

| 跳 | 本实例的实现 |
|:--|:--|
| L0 → L1 | 恒等（`Data = List ℝ`） |
| L1 → L2 | `encodeForm` / `decodePayload`（上一轮的往返定理） |
| L2 → L3 | 线性形式 ↦ 其残差的平方 |
| 语义 | `satSym`：残差为零；`satW`：损失为零 |
stmt:
noncomputable def linearLadder (n : ℕ) :
    Lattice.Lift.Ladder (List ℝ) ℝ (Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) ℝ where
  l0l1
proof:
identityTokenizer ℝ
  l1l2 :=
    { encode := fun c => (encodeForm c).payload
      decode := fun rs => decodePayload n rs
      roundtrip := fun c => L1L2Roundtrip.decodePayload_encodeForm n c }
  l2l3 := fun c => (linearResid c (fun _ => 0)) ^ 2
  satSym := fun c => linearResid c (fun _ => 0) = 0
  satW := fun L => L = 0
  l2l3_sound := by
    intro s hs
    show (linearResid s (fun _ => 0)) ^ 2 = 0
    rw [hs]
    ring

name: linearLadder_forward
doc:
**实例的第一个推论：正向保语义。**

`linearLadder` 满足的 `ladder_forward`，把「符号形式满足约束」推到「末端 artifact 满足」。
这条定理在 `Ladder` 有实例之前是空转的。
stmt:
theorem linearLadder_forward (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n)
    (hsat : (linearLadder n).satSym c) : (linearLadder n).satW ((linearLadder n).l2l3 c)
proof: Ladder.ladder_forward (linearLadder n) c hsat

name: linearLadder_l1l2_roundtrip
doc: **实例的往返性质**：L1 → L2 的编码被解码回原形式。
stmt:
theorem linearLadder_l1l2_roundtrip (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) :
    (linearLadder n).l1l2.decode ((linearLadder n).l1l2.encode c) = some c
proof:
Tokenizer.decode_encode (linearLadder n).l1l2 c

end LadderInstance

end Lattice.Geo

name: seg_smul_iff
doc:
**`seg` expressed as a scalar multiple agrees with `Plücker`'s `•` form.**

The two files describe scalar multiples in the idioms their own proofs preferred -- `fun i => t * f i` in
`Constraint`, `t • f` in `Plucker` -- and this lemma is where they meet. It is `funext` plus `Pi.smul_apply`.
stmt:
theorem seg_smul_iff (u v : Pt n) :
    (∃ t : ℝ, u = fun i => t * v i) ↔ (∃ t : ℝ, u = t • v)
proof:
by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
    exact ⟨t, by ext i; simp [ht, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]⟩
  · rintro ⟨t, ht⟩
    exact ⟨t, by ext i; simp [ht, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]⟩

name: collinearPenalty_eq_zero_iff_of_ne
doc:
**`collinearPenalty` vanishes exactly on collinear configurations**, off the degenerate locus.

The hypothesis `seg c a ≠ 0` is what makes the two orientations of dependence equivalent: if
`seg b a = t • seg c a` the constraint holds outright, and if `seg c a = t • seg b a` with `seg c a` non-zero then
`seg b a = (1/t) • seg c a`. Without it the second orientation could occur with `seg b a` alone non-zero, which the
constraint's `∃` does not permit.
stmt:
theorem collinearPenalty_eq_zero_iff_of_ne (a b c : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hne : GeoConstraint.seg pts a c ≠ 0) :
    collinearPenalty a b c pts = 0 ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds (.collinear a b c) pts
proof:
by
  unfold collinearPenalty
  rw [pluckerNorm_eq_zero_iff]
  constructor
  ·                                                                 
    rintro ⟨t, h | h⟩
    · exact (seg_smul_iff _ _).mpr ⟨t, h⟩
    ·                                                             
      have ht : t ≠ 0 := by
        rintro rfl
        apply hne
        rw [h]
        ext i
        simp [Pi.smul_apply]
      refine (seg_smul_iff _ _).mpr ⟨t⁻¹, ?_⟩
      rw [h]
      ext i
      simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
      field_simp
  ·                                                     
    intro h
    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := (seg_smul_iff _ _).mp h
    exact ⟨t, Or.inl ht⟩

name: parallelPenalty_eq_zero_iff_of_ne
doc:
**`parallelPenalty` vanishes exactly on parallel configurations**, off the degenerate locus.

Same statement and same proof as `collinear`; named separately because the constraint is, and because a reader
looking for one should not have to travel through the other.
stmt:
theorem parallelPenalty_eq_zero_iff_of_ne (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hne : GeoConstraint.seg pts c e ≠ 0) :
    parallelPenalty a b c e pts = 0 ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds (.parallel a b c e) pts
proof:
by
  unfold parallelPenalty
  rw [pluckerNorm_eq_zero_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨t, h | h⟩
    · exact (seg_smul_iff _ _).mpr ⟨t, h⟩
    · have ht : t ≠ 0 := by
        rintro rfl
        apply hne
        rw [h]
        ext i
        simp [Pi.smul_apply]
      refine (seg_smul_iff _ _).mpr ⟨t⁻¹, ?_⟩
      rw [h]
      ext i
      simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
      field_simp
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := (seg_smul_iff _ _).mp h
    exact ⟨t, Or.inl ht⟩

name: ptIndex
doc: 索引集：`range k × univ`（点号 × 坐标）。
stmt: def ptIndex (n k : ℕ) : Finset (ℕ × Fin n)
proof: Finset.range k ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))

name: rho
doc:
**点列在前缀上的偏差。**

`k = 0` 或 `n = 0` 时索引集为空，取值 `0`。
stmt: noncomputable def rho (n k : ℕ) (pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n) : ℝ
proof:
if h : (ptIndex n k).Nonempty
  then (ptIndex n k).sup' (f := fun pi => |pts pi.1 pi.2 - pts' pi.1 pi.2|) h
  else 0

name: rho_nonneg
stmt: theorem rho_nonneg (n k : ℕ) (pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n) : 0 ≤ rho n k pts pts'
proof:
by
  unfold rho
  split
  · next h =>
    obtain ⟨x, _hx, hfx⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' h
      (fun pi : ℕ × Fin n => |pts pi.1 pi.2 - pts' pi.1 pi.2|)
    rw [hfx]
    exact abs_nonneg _
  · exact le_rfl

name: abs_coord_sub_le_rho
doc: 前缀内的单个坐标差不超过 `rho`。
proof:
by
  have hmem : (p, i) ∈ ptIndex n k :=
    Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_range.mpr hp, Finset.mem_univ _⟩
  have hne : (ptIndex n k).Nonempty := ⟨(p, i), hmem⟩
  unfold rho
  rw [dif_pos hne]
  exact Finset.le_sup' (f := fun pi => |pts pi.1 pi.2 - pts' pi.1 pi.2|) hmem

name: LipschitzK
doc: **`LipschitzK e K`**：`e` 在偏差 `rho` 下以 `K` 为 Lipschitz 常数。
stmt: def LipschitzK (n k : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (K : ℝ) : Prop
proof:
∀ pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n,
    |GeoExpr.evalPts e pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e pts'| ≤ K * rho n k pts pts'

name: BoundedV
doc: **`BoundedV e B`**：`e` 的取值被 `B` 界住。
stmt: def BoundedV (n : ℕ) (e : GeoExpr n) (B : ℝ) : Prop
proof: ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n, |GeoExpr.evalPts e pts| ≤ B

name: lipschitz_coord
doc: **`coord p axis`** 是 `1`-Lipschitz（在前缀内）。
stmt:
theorem lipschitz_coord (n k : ℕ) (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (hp : p < k) :
    LipschitzK n k (.coord p axis) 1
proof:
by
  intro pts pts'
  have h := abs_coord_sub_le_rho (n := n) (k := k) (pts := pts) (pts' := pts') (p := p)
    (i := axis) hp
  simpa [LipschitzK, GeoExpr.evalPts] using h

name: lipschitz_const
doc: **`const c`** 是 `0`-Lipschitz。
stmt: theorem lipschitz_const (n k : ℕ) (c : ℝ) : LipschitzK n k (.const c) 0
proof:
by
  intro pts pts'
  simp [LipschitzK, GeoExpr.evalPts]

name: boundedV_const
doc: **`const c`** 的值域界是 `|c|`。
stmt: theorem boundedV_const (n : ℕ) (c : ℝ) : BoundedV n (.const c) |c|
proof:
by
  intro pts
  simp [BoundedV, GeoExpr.evalPts]

name: lipschitz_add
doc: **`add`**：常数 `K₁ + K₂`。
proof:
by
  intro pts pts'
  have h1 := h₁ pts pts'
  have h2 := h₂ pts pts'
  have heq : GeoExpr.evalPts (.add e₁ e₂) pts - GeoExpr.evalPts (.add e₁ e₂) pts'
      = (GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts')
        + (GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts') := by
    simp [GeoExpr.evalPts]; ring
  rw [heq]
  calc |(GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts')
          + (GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts')|
      ≤ |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts'|
          + |GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'| := abs_add _ _
    _ ≤ K₁ * rho n k pts pts' + K₂ * rho n k pts pts' := by linarith
    _ = (K₁ + K₂) * rho n k pts pts' := by ring

name: boundedV_add
doc: **`add`** 的值域界：`B₁ + B₂`。
proof:
by
  intro pts
  have h1 := h₁ pts
  have h2 := h₂ pts
  have heq : |GeoExpr.evalPts (.add e₁ e₂) pts|
      = |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts + GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts| := by rfl
  rw [heq]
  calc |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts + GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts|
      ≤ |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts| + |GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts| := abs_add _ _
    _ ≤ B₁ + B₂ := by linarith

name: lipschitz_sub
doc: **`sub`**：常数 `K₁ + K₂`。
proof:
by
  intro pts pts'
  have h1 := h₁ pts pts'
  have h2 := h₂ pts pts'
  have heq : GeoExpr.evalPts (.sub e₁ e₂) pts - GeoExpr.evalPts (.sub e₁ e₂) pts'
      = (GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts')
        - (GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts') := by
    simp [GeoExpr.evalPts]; ring
  rw [heq]
  calc |(GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts')
          - (GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts')|
      ≤ |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts'|
          + |GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'| := abs_sub _ _
    _ ≤ K₁ * rho n k pts pts' + K₂ * rho n k pts pts' := by linarith
    _ = (K₁ + K₂) * rho n k pts pts' := by ring

name: boundedV_sub
doc: **`sub`** 的值域界：`B₁ + B₂`。
proof:
by
  intro pts
  have h1 := h₁ pts
  have h2 := h₂ pts
  have heq : |GeoExpr.evalPts (.sub e₁ e₂) pts|
      = |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts| := by rfl
  rw [heq]
  calc |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts|
      ≤ |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts| + |GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts| := abs_sub _ _
    _ ≤ B₁ + B₂ := by linarith

name: lipschitz_mul
doc:
**`mul`**：常数 `K₁·B₂ + K₂·B₁`。

关键插项：`f·g - f'·g' = f·(g - g') + (f - f')·g'`。
第一项用 `|f| ≤ B₁`，第二项用 `|g'| ≤ B₂`。
**这就是归纳必须携带值域界的原因**。
stmt:
theorem lipschitz_mul {n k : ℕ} {e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n} {K₁ K₂ B₁ B₂ : ℝ}
    (hl₁ : LipschitzK n k e₁ K₁) (hl₂ : LipschitzK n k e₂ K₂)
    (hb₁ : BoundedV n e₁ B₁) (hb₂ : BoundedV n e₂ B₂)
    (hB₁ : 0 ≤ B₁) (hB₂ : 0 ≤ B₂) (hK₁ : 0 ≤ K₁) :
    LipschitzK n k (.mul e₁ e₂) (K₁ * B₂ + K₂ * B₁)
proof:
by
  intro pts pts'
  have hρ := rho_nonneg n k pts pts'
  have h1 := hl₁ pts pts'
  have h2 := hl₂ pts pts'
  have hv1 := hb₁ pts
  have hv2 := hb₂ pts'
  have heq : GeoExpr.evalPts (.mul e₁ e₂) pts - GeoExpr.evalPts (.mul e₁ e₂) pts'
      = GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts * (GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts')
        + (GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts') * GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts' := by
    simp [GeoExpr.evalPts]; ring
  rw [heq]
  have htri : |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts * (GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts')
        + (GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts') * GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'|
      ≤ |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts| * |GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'|
        + |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts'| * |GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'| := by
    calc |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts * (GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts')
            + (GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts') * GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'|
        ≤ |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts * (GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts')|
            + |(GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts') * GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'| :=
          abs_add _ _
      _ = |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts| * |GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'|
            + |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts'| * |GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts'| := by
          rw [abs_mul, abs_mul]
  refine htri.trans ?_

name: boundedV_mul
doc: **`mul`** 的值域界：`B₁ · B₂`。
proof:
by
  intro pts
  have h1 := h₁ pts
  have h2 := h₂ pts
  have heq : |GeoExpr.evalPts (.mul e₁ e₂) pts|
      = |GeoExpr.evalPts e₁ pts * GeoExpr.evalPts e₂ pts| := by rfl
  rw [heq, abs_mul]
  exact mul_le_mul h1 h2 (abs_nonneg _) (le_trans (abs_nonneg _) h1)

end Lattice.Geo

name: fixSamePoint
doc: **Copy one point's coordinates onto another.** The repair step for `samePoint a b`.
stmt: noncomputable def fixSamePoint (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : ℕ → Pt n
proof: Function.update pts b (pts a)

name: fixSamePoint_self
doc: The repaired point reads back as `a`'s value -- by `update_same`, with no `if` to unfold.
stmt:
